(Script: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/pat.mjs, run with deno run --allow-read.)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Extend the patterns: allow an optional path and prefixes after the pipe (`\|\s*(?:sudo\s+|nohup\s+|env\s+)*(?:\S*/)?(?:ba|z|da|k)?sh\b`), add `(?:ba|z)?sh\s+<\(\s*(?:curl|wget)`, `\$\([^)]{0,200}base64\s+(?:-d|--decode|-D)`, `\bfinger\b[^\n|]{0,100}\|\s*cmd`, a UNC/WebDAV rule (`^\s*\\\\[^\\\s]+(?:@ssl|@\d+)?\\` and `davwwwroot`), UNC paths for msiexec/regsvr32, and `powershell ... -f(?:ile)? \\\\`. Add each string as a test case in test/guards.test.js.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by re-running docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/pat.mjs against the real PATTERNS. These strings are missed: '| /bin/bash', '| nohup bash', 'bash <(curl ...)', '/bin/bash -c "$(echo b64 | base64 -d)"', 'cmd /c "finger x@host | cmd"', the WebDAV UNC '\\host@SSL\DavWWWRoot\x.exe', msiexec and regsvr32 with a UNC path, and 'powershell -ep bypass -f \\host\a.ps1'. curl-pipe-shell (clipboard.js:100) needs the bare shell name right after the pipe. msiexec-remote and regsvr32 need http(s). Several of these forms (finger | cmd, a WebDAV path pasted into Run, a pipe to /bin/bash) are used in documented ClickFix campaigns. A pattern list can never be complete, and each pattern is a single gap that is easy to fix, so I rate it medium.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The patterns are a deliberate heuristic list kept narrow to avoid false positives (for example, SAFE_HOSTS exists because install commands like 'curl | sh' are legitimate). Nothing in CHANGELOG/TODO marks these variants as excluded on purpose. The 0.3.5 changelog extended the list (irm | iex, bash -c "$(curl)"), which shows that extending it is the intended way forward.
verdict.fix_notes: In PATTERNS (clipboard.js:85-105): change curl-pipe-shell to /\b(?:curl|wget)\b[^\n|]{0,300}\|\s*(?:(?:sudo|nohup|env)\s+)*(?:\S*\/)?(?:ba|z|da|k)?sh\b/i. Add a process-substitution rule /\b(?:ba|z)?sh\s+<\(\s*(?:curl|wget)\b/i. Widen shell-c-download to accept a base64 decode inside $(...): /\b(?:ba|z|da)?sh\s+-c\s+["']?\$\([^)]{0,300}base64\s+(?:-d|--decode|-D)/i. Add finger-pipe-cmd /\bfinger(?:\.exe)?\b[^\n|]{0,100}\|\s*cmd\b/i. Add a webdav-unc rule limited to WebDAV markers or executable extensions, to avoid matching plain intranet share paths: /\\\\[^\\\s]+@(?:ssl|\d+)\\|\bdavwwwroot\b/i. Let msiexec, regsvr32 and powershell -f(ile) accept '\\\\' as well as https?:. Keep every gap bounded so matching stays linear. Add every missed string as a positive case in the clipboard pattern tests (test/guards.test.js), and add negatives such as 'cat file | bash-completion' and '\\fileserver\share\doc.pdf'.

confirmed.title: Popup guard: pop-unders and second windows through <a target=_blank>.click() or a form with target=_blank are not checked
confirmed.description: The guard wraps only window.open. A page can open a new tab from a click on plain content with a created anchor (target=_blank) and a.click(), or with form.target='_blank' and submit(). Chrome allows both with the click's activation. The 'second window in one click' rule is also bypassed: one window.open plus one anchor click opens two windows.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
Guard switched on. A click handler on a

with plain text runs: const a=document.createElement('a'); a.href='http://other-site/ad'; a.target='_blank'; a.click(). Result: a new tab opens on the other site. The same handler with window.open is blocked (control).
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/p1.mjs (Chrome 153, extension loaded, settings.features.guardPopups = true). Output:
`control: window.open from plain content blocked`
`popunder via <a target=_blank>.click() OPENED 1: http://localhost:.../ad`
`popunder via form target=_blank submit OPENED 1`
`control: second window.open in one click (button) OPENED 1`
`second window via window.open + a.click (button) OPENED 2`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also judge anchor and form navigations that open a new browsing context: a capture listener on window for 'click' events whose composedPath() starts at an <a>/<area> with target other than _self/_parent/_top that was not the trusted clicked node, wrap HTMLElement.prototype.click for anchors and HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit/requestSubmit when target opens a new window, and count these in `opens`. Or document clearly that only window.open is covered.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with p1.mjs (guardPopups=true): '<a target=_blank>.click()' and 'form target=_blank submit' from a click on plain content both open a cross-site tab, while window.open in the same case is blocked. window.open plus a.click opens 2 windows where two window.open calls open 1. The guard (popups.js:250-276) wraps only win.open. Pop-under scripts often use a created anchor with .click(). The feature is off by default, and docs/how-it-works.md:52 states the scope as 'Blocks `window.open` without a click...'. So this is a coverage gap of an opt-in feature, and I rate it low.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The documented scope is window.open only (docs/how-it-works.md:52, the popups.js header). The feature is off by default because 'false positives are likely'. Covering anchor and form navigation would raise that risk. I found no explicit decision to exclude anchors.
verdict.fix_notes: Option A: wrap HTMLElement.prototype.click (or HTMLAnchorElement/HTMLAreaElement click) and HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit/requestSubmit. When the element's target (read through captured getters) is not ''/_self/_parent/_top and the href or action is cross-site, run judge() with the same ctx as window.open. If it blocks, do nothing and signal(); if it allows, count it in `opens`. Also add a window capture 'click' listener: a synthetic (isTrusted false) click on such an anchor goes through the same check (preventDefault when blocked). Option B: document in docs/how-it-works.md and the popups.js header that only window.open is covered. Add Chrome tests from p1.mjs.

confirmed.title: Popup guard: window.open of a same-origin frame skips the pop-under check (per-frame click state, and the switch is off until flags arrive)
confirmed.description: Each frame has its own guard with its own lastClick and its own switch. 1) The switch starts as false (line 287) and comes later from chrome.storage through flags.js, so in a new about:blank frame used at once the guard is off. 2) After the flags arrive, the frame's navigator.userActivation.isActive is true (activation from the parent click), but the frame's lastClick is null because the click happened in the parent realm, so judge() never returns 'popunder' or 'second window'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Guard on. A click handler on plain page text runs: const f=document.createElement('iframe'); document.body.appendChild(f); f.contentWindow.open('http://other-site/ad') (at once, or 300 ms later). Result: the tab opens. The same open from the top window is blocked as 'popunder (click on page content)'.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/p3.mjs. Output:
`plain content: fresh frame, open at once OPENED`
`plain content: fresh frame, open after 300 ms OPENED`
`plain content: top window.open after 300 ms blocked`
Trace with console.log added to a scratch copy of popups.js: `enter flag false about:blank` (first case) and `about:blank flag true act true reason null` (second case). p2.mjs shows the frame's open is the guard's Proxy (`function () { [native code] }`), so this is not an injection-timing gap.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In an about:blank/srcdoc/blob: frame (or any same-origin child frame), take the gesture state from the top same-origin ancestor: read the parent guard's state through a private channel, or have the top guard also wrap window.open of same-origin child frames it can reach. For a frame without its own click in the last 5 s while isActive is true, treat the open as a pop-under. Consider default 'on' until flags arrive when the stored setting is on (cache the last value in sessionStorage is not safe; better resolve the flag synchronously from a value flags.js writes at injection).

verdict.reason: Confirmed with p3.mjs: a fresh same-origin iframe's contentWindow.open from a click on plain content opens a tab, both at once and 300 ms later, while a top-window open in the same case is blocked. Each realm has its own lastClick (popups.js:181). The trusted click is dispatched only in the parent realm. The child realm's navigator.userActivation.isActive is true, because Chrome copies activation to same-origin descendants, but its lastClick is null. So judge() never reaches the popunder or second-window rules. Also, `on` starts false (287) until the flag port answers, so a frame used at once is not guarded. The popunder rule has a simple bypass. The feature is off by default, so I rate it low.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: Per-frame guards with injection into about:blank/srcdoc/blob frames (match_about_blank) were added so that a page 'cannot reach a pristine window.open through a blank frame'. That design covers the native method, not shared gesture state. Starting with the switch off matches the feature's default-off setting. No comment covers the gesture state of a parent realm.
verdict.fix_notes: In install() (popups.js), when win !== win.top and the parent is same-origin (try to read win.parent.location.href), find the gesture state of the nearest same-origin ancestor. Option: the top guard stores {lastClick, opens} in a closure, and the top guard wraps window.open of same-origin child frames it can reach (from a MutationObserver on iframe insertion, or by patching the HTMLIFrameElement.prototype.contentWindow getter to wrap the child's open with the top's judge). Simpler fallback: in a child frame, if activation is true and this realm saw no trusted pointerdown/mousedown/click/keydown in the last 5 s, judge the open as 'popunder (gesture in another frame)' for cross-site targets. For the switch: when flags have not arrived yet, the frame can read the flag value from the parent same-origin guard. Add Chrome tests from p3.mjs.

confirmed.title: Popup guard false positive: a keyboard-started window.open within 5 s of a click in a text field is blocked as a pop-under
confirmed.description: Gestures are tracked only from pointerdown, mousedown and click. A keydown gesture does not reset lastClick. INTERACTIVE does not include text inputs or textareas. So when the visitor clicks into a search box and presses Enter within 5 s, and the site opens results in a new window from the keydown handler, the stale click on the input is judged as a click on plain content. The same open 5.5 s after the click is allowed, so the result depends only on typing speed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Guard on. Page has <input id=q> with a keydown handler that calls window.open('https://other-site/search?...') on Enter. The visitor clicks the box, types 'abc' and presses Enter. Result: blocked ('popunder (click on page content)') and the toolbar dot is set. If the visitor waits more than 5 s after the click, the window opens.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/guards-lens/p5.mjs. Output:
`click in search box, type, press Enter (keydown -> window.open) BLOCKED`
`same, but Enter pressed 5.5 s after the click opened`
`control: click Sign in button opened`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track trusted keydown (and keyup) on window in capture phase as the start of a new gesture: set lastClick to the event's target (or the focused element) and reset opens. Add input, textarea, [contenteditable] and [tabindex] to the interactive selector, or treat a gesture whose last event is a key event as interactive.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with p5.mjs: click in a search box, type, press Enter, and a keydown handler calls window.open: BLOCKED. The same open after 5.5 s is allowed, and a Sign-in button click is allowed. track() is registered only for pointerdown/mousedown/click (popups.js:241-247). INTERACTIVE (45) has no input[type=text]/textarea/[contenteditable], so a click into a text field counts as a click on plain content, and a later keyboard gesture inherits that stale state. This is a false positive in an off-by-default guard, so I rate it low.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The header says the guard is off by default because 'false positives are likely'. INTERACTIVE lists controls that are usually meant to open things, and text inputs were probably left out so that a click into a field followed by a script pop-under still counts. Keyboard gestures are not mentioned anywhere.
verdict.fix_notes: In install(), also register a trusted keydown capture listener on window. On a trusted keydown, set lastClick = {at: now(), target: activeElement (through a captured getter), interactive: true, down: false} and reset opens = 0, so that a keyboard-started gesture is never judged as a popunder. Or add 'input,textarea,[contenteditable]' to INTERACTIVE only for gestures whose latest trusted event was a key event. Add a unit test in the popups tests: click on an <input>, then keydown Enter within 5 s, then window.open(cross-site) must be allowed. Keep the existing test that a click on plain text plus window.open is blocked.

confirmed.title: A stolen feed key can set the serial to 2^31-1, and a key rotation cannot recover the feed
confirmed.description: The 1,000,000 serial-step limit (L-7) does not apply when the stored document has expired (storedExpired). The attacker controls notAfter, so one document with a very short life opens the 'any jump' path on the next check. feedState.serial is never reset: not by the kill latch release (client.js:152 RELEASED keeps serial) and not by an extension update. After the serial is 2147483647, no document can be newer (MAX_SERIAL check at schema.js:77), so the feed stays dead for every existing install, also after the owner ships new pinned keys. docs/feed-setup.md says to ship new keys in an update as the recovery. That recovery does not work.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Stored serial 5. Check 1: attacker serves serial 6 with notAfter = now+60 s (accepted). Check 2, 3 h later: stored doc has expired, attacker serves serial 2147483647 (accepted, no step limit). Owner signs a kill document (accepted), then ships an update with a new feed key. Every new feed signed with the new key is rejected: 'serial 2147483647 is not newer than 2147483647 (replay or rollback attack)', also 15, 30 and 45 days later. A publisher typo (serial 2147483647) gives the same permanent lock without an attacker.
confirmed.evidence: Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/repro.test.mjs test A (harness docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/harness.mjs, copied from test/feed-client.test.js). Output: 'atk1 ... applied 6', 'atk2 ... applied 2147483647', 'kill ... killed', 'new key feed {"ok":false,... "serial 2147483647 is not newer than 2147483647 (replay or rollback attack)"}', and the same reason on three later checks. Code: schema.js:97 checkSerialBound(doc.serial, c.storedSerial, "serial", ...storedNotAfter > 0 && nowForBound >= c.storedNotAfter); schema.js:78 skips the step check when storedExpired; client.js:250 storedSerial: st.serial; client.js:152 RELEASED has no serial reset.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Bind the stored serial to the key that signed it: store serial per keyId (or reset st.serial, st.notAfter and the cache when the signing keyId is no longer pinned, or when the kill latch is released by an update). Measure the expiry escape from a minimum lifetime (for example only when the stored doc lived at least 24 h), or remove the escape and allow the step only after N consecutive checks. Add a test: kill, then update with a new key, then serial 1 from the new key is accepted.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by re-running docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/repro.test.mjs test A: serial 6 with a 60 s life, then 2147483647 after it expires; both are accepted. After a kill and a feed signed with a new key, every check rejects with 'serial 2147483647 is not newer than 2147483647'. Code: schema.js:97 skips the step limit when storedExpired, and the attacker sets notAfter. client.js:152 RELEASED keeps st.serial. client.js:250 passes st.serial for any key. So the documented recovery (docs/feed-setup.md 'Emergency switches': ship new pinned keys in an update) cannot work. feed-sign.mjs:36 validates with storedSerial 0 and accepts 2147483647, so a publisher typo gives the same lock. Rated down from high to medium: the feed is dormant in 0.3.5 (FEED_ORIGIN is empty), and the attack needs a stolen feed key or a publisher typo. Without the escape, a stolen key also needs about 2,147 checks (about 268 days) to reach the cap.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: schema.js:72-74 comment: the expiry escape is on purpose, so 'a publisher who changes the serial scheme must not lock browsers out for good'. CHANGELOG 0.3.x adds the 2^31-1 cap and the 1,000,000 step limit as hardening. Nothing shows that the interaction with key rotation was considered: the git history is one squashed commit, and no doc mentions a serial reset.
verdict.fix_notes: In client.js, record the keyId that verified the stored feed (have verifyFeed return keyId, and store st.serialKeyId). In checkFeed and applyCached: when st.serialKeyId is no longer in the pinned FEED_KEYS, or when RELEASED is applied after a kill, reset serial, notAfter and appliedSerial to 0 and clear the cache. Also allow the expiry escape only when the stored document lived at least 24 h (store notBefore and check notAfter - notBefore >= 24 h). In feed-sign.mjs, warn when a serial is above about 2^31 - 10^7. Tests in test/feed-client.test.js: (a) kill, update with a new key, then serial 1 signed with the new key is accepted; (b) a stored doc with a 60 s life that expires does not open a 2^31-1 jump.

confirmed.title: Storage write failure after the rule swap: the next worker start puts back the old (possibly bad) rules
confirmed.description: checkFeed applies the new session rules first (289), then writes the cache (290) and then the state (291). The comment covers only a failed rule update. When setCache throws (QUOTA_BYTES), the new rules are active but feedCache.current is still the old document and feedState.serial is old. applyCached runs at every MV3 worker start (general-background.js:970) and re-applies cache.current, so the rules flip back to the old document within about 30 s of idle. This also undoes a killFeed:true or rollback document that the publisher sent to remove a bad rule. The storage budget makes this reachable: the budget test (test/final-storage-budget.test.js) allows a 9,000,000-byte list peak and does not count the feed cache. Two 512 KB feeds are stored as base64: 2 x 699,052 = 1,398,104 bytes, total 10,398,104 of the 10,485,760 quota before feedState and other keys.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Cached feed serial 1 blocks old.example. Feed serial 2 (blocks new.example only) arrives; setCache throws QUOTA_BYTES. Rules now: new.example, state serial 1. The worker sleeps and wakes: applyCached re-applies serial 1, rules now old.example. Popup shows 'serial 1' the whole time. If serial 2 was killFeed:true to remove a false positive on a bank, the false positive comes back at every worker start until a check succeeds.
confirmed.evidence: Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/repro2.test.mjs test F: 'check {"ok":false,..."QUOTA_BYTES quota exceeded"} rules now [ "new.example" ] state serial 1 status active' then 'worker restart {"ok":true,"mode":"cache","rules":1} rules now [ "old.example" ]'. Test G prints 'two 1398104 plus PEAK_LIMIT 9e6 = 10398104 quota 10485760'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Write the cache before the rule swap (or roll the rules back when setCache throws), so the cache always matches the active rules. Store the feed cache as raw text instead of base64, or keep only one previous entry, and add the feed cache to the storage budget test.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by re-running repro2 test F: setCache throws QUOTA_BYTES after replaceRules (client.js:289-290). The rules show new.example while state and cache still hold serial 1. The next applyCached (general-background.js:970 runs at every worker start) puts old.example back. The catch at client.js:293 records only lastError. Test G arithmetic: two base64 cache entries of 512 KB each are 1,398,104 bytes, and the budget test does not count them. Rated down to low: the feed is dormant, the failure needs the quota to be nearly full, and real feeds are much smaller than 512 KB. The state stays consistent with the cache. The live rules alone differ from the cache, until the next check succeeds.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: client.js:287-288 comment 'Rules first, storage second: if the rule update throws (quota), the stored serial does not advance and the old rules stay active.' The order was chosen for a replaceRules failure. The setCache failure case was not covered.
verdict.fix_notes: In checkFeed's normal path, wrap setCache. When it throws, call replaceRules with the rules compiled from the verified cache.current (or remove the feed rules for a killFeed doc), then record lastError, so the rules always match the cache. Do the same in the rollback path. Optionally store the bytes as text, not base64. Add the feed cache (2 x 512 KB worst case) to test/final-storage-budget.test.js. Test: setCache throws -> the active session rules equal the cached document's rules.

confirmed.title: Kill serial has a permanent step limit with no expiry escape: a second kill can be refused for ever
confirmed.description: validateKill calls checkSerialBound without the storedExpired argument, so a kill serial may never jump more than 1,000,000 above the last stored kill serial. killSerial is kept across the latch release (client.js:152). docs/feed-setup.md recommends date-like serials (2026111001) for feeds. If the publisher uses the same style for kill serials, a second kill more than about one year later is rejected and the feed stays active. The kill key is the emergency switch for a stolen feed key, so this fails open at the worst time. feed-sign.mjs validates kill documents with storedKillSerial 0, so it signs the document without a warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Kill serial 2026111001 is accepted and later released by an update. 400 days later the feed key is stolen; the owner signs kill serial 2027121501. Every browser that saw the first kill answers 'kill serial jumps from 2026111001 to 2027121501 (more than 1000000)' and keeps the attacker's feed rules.
confirmed.evidence: Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/repro.test.mjs test C: 'kill1 killed', 'feed applied [ "x.example" ]', 'kill2 {"ok":false,..."kill serial jumps from 2026111001 to 2027121501 (more than 1000000)"} [ "x.example" ]'. Code: schema.js:190 checkSerialBound(doc.serial, c.storedKillSerial, "kill serial") with no 4th argument.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Remove the step limit for kill documents (the kill key can only switch the feed off, so a high kill serial cannot hurt anybody), or document and enforce a small counter (1, 2, 3) for kill serials in feed-setup.md and in feed-sign.mjs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by repro test C. schema.js:190 calls checkSerialBound with no expiry escape, and client.js:152 RELEASED keeps killSerial. A second kill whose serial is more than 1,000,000 above the first is refused for ever, and the feed stays on. docs/feed-setup.md:77-79 says that date-like feed serials are fine and gives no rule for kill serials. The example at line 46 uses serial 1, so the problem occurs only if the publisher uses date-like kill serials. feed-sign.mjs:33 validates with storedKillSerial 0 and gives no warning. The kill key can only switch the feed off, so the step limit protects almost nothing. Low: the feed is dormant, and the problem needs a publisher choice.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: CHANGELOG (latch release) says 'serials are capped at 2^31-1 and may not jump more than 1,000,000'. The rule was applied to both document types the same way. No reason is given for kill documents.
verdict.fix_notes: In schema.js validateKill, remove the step check (keep only the MAX_SERIAL cap and serial > storedKillSerial), or pass storedExpired=true. Add to docs/feed-setup.md: 'kill serials: any increasing number'. Test: storedKillSerial 2026111001, kill serial 2027121501 is accepted.

confirmed.title: Threat tier switched off, feed on: the feed fallback snapshot installs the whole packed threat list again
confirmed.description: feedPaused is computed as !(s.enabled && s.features.threatFeed); it ignores threatTier. When the feed has no valid cached document (fresh install, expired, after a kill release), applyCached installs src/rules/threat-snapshot.json as session rules (client.js:193). That snapshot is built from the packed threat set, which is exactly the list the user switched off with 'Block known malware hosts'. The settings page tells the user 'packed threat list off too' (settings.js:91). Latent while the feed is dormant; becomes active when FEED_ORIGIN is set.
confirmed.failure_scenario: User switches off 'Block known malware hosts' (threatTier) because the threat list blocks a site they need; threatFeed stays on (default). Feed configured, cache expired. Worker starts: applyCached installs 199 snapshot rules (about 15,925 hosts) at priority 2,000,010. The site stays blocked although the user switched the threat tier off and the page says the packed list is off.
confirmed.evidence: general-background.js:315 'const paused = !(s.enabled && s.features.threatFeed);'. client.js:193-195 snapshotRules -> replaceRules, state source 'snapshot'. src/feed/schema.js:168-170 says the snapshot is built from the packed threat set. Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/perf.test.mjs shows applyCached with no cache installs the snapshot (session updates 20 for 20 starts).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not use the snapshot fallback when threatTier is off (pass threatTier to the feed deps, or include it in the pause condition for the snapshot path only). Add a test: threatTier off + feed configured + no cache -> no session rules.

verdict.reason: general-background.js:315 pauses the feed only on enabled/threatFeed and ignores threatTier. client.js:193-195 installs threat-snapshot.json, which is built from the packed threat set (schema.js:166-170), when no valid cache exists. So with threatTier off and threatFeed on, the same hosts that the user switched off are blocked again at priority 2,000,010. settings.js:91 tells the user 'packed threat list off too' only for the fallback text. Low: the code path does nothing until FEED_ORIGIN is set (applyCached returns 'dormant' first).
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The snapshot is meant as the feed's offline fallback (docs/feed-setup.md:25, CHANGELOG feed client entry). The designers may have treated it as part of the feed, not of the threat tier, but no doc says that threatTier off should leave these hosts blocked.
verdict.fix_notes: In general-background.js, pass threatTier into the feed deps (for example deps.getSnapshotAllowed = () => threatOn). In client.js applyCached, when no valid cache exists and the snapshot is not allowed, call removeFeedRules and set the state source 'none' instead of installing the snapshot. Also call applyCachedFeed when threatTier changes. Test: threatTier off + configured feed + no cache -> 0 session rules.

confirmed.title: A re-served rollback document gives a false 'replay or rollback attack' warning at every check
confirmed.description: The 0.3.5 fix for the false replay warning compares the fetched bytes with cache.current. After a rollback, cache.current is the rolled-back-to entry (client.js:281), not the rollback document, and st.serial is the rollback document's serial. The publisher keeps serving the rollback document (the normal case), so every 3-hour check fails the unchanged test, goes to verifyFeed and is rejected as a replay. fetchedAt does not move. The same happens after a 'rollback target not stored' answer (client.js:274).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Serials 1 and 2 applied, then rollback document 3 (rollbackTo 1) applied. Next check with the same files: lastError 'rejected: serial 3 is not newer than 3 (replay or rollback attack)'; the popup shows this as the last problem until the publisher signs a new feed. A real attack warning becomes noise.
confirmed.evidence: Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/repro.test.mjs test D: 'rb rollback', then 'recheck {"ok":false,"ran":true,"reason":"serial 3 is not newer than 3 (replay or rollback attack)"} ... fetchedAt: false'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the sig and bytes hash of the last accepted document (also rollback documents) in feedState, and treat an identical re-served document as 'unchanged'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by repro test D. After a rollback, cache.current is the rollback target (client.js:281), and st.serial (3) != st.appliedSerial (1). So the unchanged short-cut at client.js:239-244 never matches. The re-served rollback document goes to verifyFeed and is rejected as a 'replay or rollback attack' at every check, and fetchedAt does not move. The same happens after 'rollback target not stored'. This is noise in the status only. The rules stay correct.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The 0.3.5 unchanged short-cut was written for the normal re-serve case only. No comment covers rollback documents.
verdict.fix_notes: In checkFeed, after a rollback document is accepted (or ignored as 'not stored'), store a hash of its bytes and sig in feedState (lastDocHash). Before verifyFeed, if the hash of the fetched bytes and sig equals st.lastDocHash, record a successful check (lastError '', fetchedAt now) and return 'unchanged'. Test: rollback applied, the same files are served again -> ok 'unchanged', no lastError.

confirmed.title: Every worker start re-verifies the feed and rewrites all feed session rules and feedState
confirmed.description: applyCached runs at the top level of the worker (general-background.js:970), so it runs at every MV3 worker wake-up, not only on browser start or update. Session rules survive a worker restart, but applyCached still re-verifies the signature, re-validates up to 512 KB, replaces all feed rules through the DNR queue and writes feedState (which fires storage.onChanged in open popups and settings pages). With no valid cache it validates the 15,925-host snapshot each time.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Feed configured, cache expired: each worker wake costs about 85 ms of CPU and one updateSessionRules call in the shared DNR queue, many times per hour, and can delay a user click that waits on the same queue.
confirmed.evidence: Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/perf.test.mjs: 'ms per applyCached 84.5 session updates 20' for 20 starts.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In applyCached, skip the rewrite when getSessionRules already holds feed rules for st.appliedSerial (or keep a session-storage marker), and run the full apply only on onStartup/onInstalled or when the rules are missing.

verdict.reason: general-background.js:970 calls applyCachedFeed at the top level, so it runs at every MV3 worker wake. The comment at 968-969 says 'Session rules die with the browser and on extension update', but session rules survive a worker restart, so the work is redundant on most wakes: re-verify the signature, re-validate up to 512 KB or the 199-rule snapshot, call updateSessionRules in the shared DNR queue, and write feedState, which fires storage.onChanged. The reviewer's measure is 84.5 ms per call in the Deno harness. This is not an issue now: the feed is dormant, and applyCached then returns early at 'dormant', with a feedState write only when the state changes.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: Comment at general-background.js:968-969: the choice is on purpose for robustness ('on every start'). It makes sure that the rules exist after a browser restart and after an update, and it does not track whether this is a cold start or a worker wake.
verdict.fix_notes: In client.js applyCached, call chrome.declarativeNetRequest.getSessionRules through deps first. If feed-range rules (ids in the feed block) exist and st.appliedSerial and st.source match what would be applied, skip replaceRules and setState. Alternatively, keep a chrome.storage.session marker that is set after a successful apply and is cleared by a browser restart. Test: two applyCached calls in a row -> one updateSessionRules call.

confirmed.title: Platform protection covers only the apex name: the hosts that serve the platform (www.facebook.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, raw.githubusercontent.com, www.dropbox.com, login.live.com) can be threat-blocked
confirmed.description: PLATFORMS (build-psl-subset.mjs:39-61) puts big shared sites in psl.js. The table() in src/threat/psl.js:37-53 protects each platform name and its PARENTS only. It does not protect children. For per-customer platforms (github.io) this is correct. For the 'big shared platforms' and CDN entries it is not correct, because the service runs on a child host: facebook.com -> www.facebook.com, jsdelivr.net -> cdn.jsdelivr.net, githubusercontent.com -> raw.githubusercontent.com, discordapp.com -> cdn.discordapp.com, dropbox.com -> www.dropbox.com, live.com -> login.live.com / outlook.live.com, wikipedia.org -> en.wikipedia.org, apple.com -> www.apple.com, amazon.com -> www.amazon.com, telegram.org -> web.telegram.org. protectedReason() (src/threat/protected-hosts.js:77-93) returns null for all of these, so compileThreatRules (src/threat/compile.js:54-61) accepts them, and the signed-feed validator (src/feed/schema.js:153) accepts them too. The rule is at priority 2,000,010, above 'Allow this page' and the stream-site allows. The comment in the generator says these entries exist because 'a host-level block would black them out', but the check does not do that.
confirmed.failure_scenario: One list line such as ||www.facebook.com^ or ||cdn.jsdelivr.net^ (a typo, a compromised upstream list, or a URLhaus entry for a shared host; see the next finding for real examples of URLhaus naming shared service hosts) is accepted by the packer or the 3-hourly refresh. Result: Facebook, or every web site that loads a library from cdn.jsdelivr.net, is blocked for all users on every page, also on YouTube/Twitch/Kick pages, and 'Allow this page' does not fix it. The growth guard (2,500 / 20%) does not stop one host.
confirmed.evidence: Scratch script docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/p3.mjs (loads psl.js, never-block-captcha.js, protected-hosts.js, compile.js and calls compileThreatRules). Output: rejected: facebook.com (shared platform facebook.com); mega.nz (shared platform mega.nz). BLOCKED at 2000010 : www.facebook.com www.instagram.com www.reddit.com en.wikipedia.org www.apple.com www.microsoft.com login.live.com outlook.live.com www.office.com www.amazon.com web.telegram.org api.x.com www.dropbox.com cdn.jsdelivr.net cdn.discordapp.com raw.githubusercontent.com dl.dropboxusercontent.com www.mediafire.com download2390.mediafire.com. docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/p2.mjs also shows protectedReason() = null for firebasestorage.googleapis.com, lh3/yt3.googleusercontent.com, challenges.cloudflare.com (Turnstile), www.recaptcha.net, js.stripe.com. psl.js:45-50 only adds parents: for (let i = 1; i < labels.length - 1; i++) reasons.set(parent, ...).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Split PLATFORMS into two groups. (a) per-customer parents (github.io, pages.dev, wixsite.com, ...): keep the current apex+parents rule. (b) single-service sites and shared CDN/service hosts: protect the name AND every host under it (same 'under' check as protected-hosts.js SUFFIX), or list the exact service hosts (www.facebook.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, raw.githubusercontent.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, cdn.discordapp.com, media.discordapp.net, dl.dropboxusercontent.com, firebasestorage.googleapis.com, login.live.com, challenges.cloudflare.com, www.recaptcha.net, ...). Add a test that compileThreatRules rejects www.<each big platform> and the named CDN hosts.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by running docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/verify-threat/v.mjs. protectedReason() returns null for www.facebook.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, raw.githubusercontent.com, login.live.com and www.amazon.com, and compileThreatRules accepts them as block rules at priority 2,000,010. Only the apex is refused ('shared platform facebook.com'). This happens because psl.js table() (lines 37-53) adds each platform name and its parents, never its children. docs/threat-tier.md says the check exists so that 'one bad list line cannot black out a whole ... platform'. For single-service sites, one line such as ||www.facebook.com^ or ||cdn.jsdelivr.net^ does black out the platform, and 'Allow this page' cannot undo it. Downgraded from high to medium. The failure is latent: today path-only lines (for example badware ||cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...^$all) are not promoted to the threat tier, and cdn.discordapp.com is not in the packed set. It needs an upstream list mistake or a bad feed entry, but nothing in this layer stops one.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The build-psl-subset.mjs header and docs/threat-tier.md describe the apex+parents rule on purpose: platforms are 'Never blocked themselves (nor their parents); their customers' subdomains still can be', so evil.github.io or d123.cloudfront.net can still be blocked. That rationale fits per-customer hosting parents. It does not fit single-service sites (facebook.com, amazon.com, live.com, wikipedia.org) or single-host CDNs (cdn.jsdelivr.net), where the children are the service itself. No comment, CHANGELOG entry or git message addresses children of those entries.
verdict.fix_notes: In scripts/build-psl-subset.mjs, split PLATFORMS into PLATFORMS_PER_CUSTOMER (github.io, pages.dev, cloudfront.net, fastly.net, googleusercontent.com, ...: keep apex+parents) and SERVICE_PLATFORMS (facebook.com, instagram.com, x.com, twitter.com, reddit.com, wikipedia.org, apple.com, microsoft.com, live.com, office.com, amazon.com, telegram.org, dropbox.com, discord.com, discordapp.com, mediafire.com, mega.nz, ...). Emit SERVICE_PLATFORMS as a new DATA field. Also emit an exact SERVICE_HOSTS list for shared CDN and service hosts whose parents hold customer content (cdn.jsdelivr.net, raw.githubusercontent.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, cdn.discordapp.com, media.discordapp.net, dl.dropboxusercontent.com, firebasestorage.googleapis.com, challenges.cloudflare.com, www.recaptcha.net, js.stripe.com). In psl.js suffixReason(), refuse any host that is under a SERVICE_PLATFORMS entry (h === p || h.endsWith('.'+p)) and any exact SERVICE_HOSTS entry. Re-run the generator, then rebuild src/rules/threat-network.json and check its rejected_by_reason in threat-meta.json. Add test cases (test/threat-tier.test.js or a psl test): compileThreatRules rejects www.facebook.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, raw.githubusercontent.com and login.live.com, and still accepts evil.github.io. Note that the allow box uses the same check, so after the change it would refuse 'www.facebook.com'. That is acceptable, but say it in the CHANGELOG.

confirmed.title: PSL subset drops every IDN (Unicode) suffix: 公司.cn, 個人.hk, 政府.hk and about 280 other ICANN suffixes can be threat-blocked and can be 'allowed' in the Allow-this-domain box
confirmed.description: The generator keeps only ASCII PSL lines: `if (!/^[!*a-z0-9.-]+$/.test(l)) continue;` with the comment 'PSL entries may be Unicode; DNR and URL hosts use punycode. Keep ASCII only.' The PSL writes IDN suffixes in Unicode, so they are dropped instead of being converted to punycode. Threat list hosts, DNR requestDomains and userDomainReason() (which converts typed Unicode with new URL(...).hostname) all use the xn-- form, and psl.js has zero xn-- names. So suffixReason/protectedReason return null for these suffixes. The ordinary list tier (isIcannSuffix) has the same gap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: (1) A list line ||xn--55qx5d.cn^ (公司.cn, the Chinese 'company' suffix) or ||xn--mxtq1m.hk^ (政府.hk, Hong Kong government) is accepted and blocks every site registered under that suffix at priority 2,000,010. (2) A user types '公司.cn' into Settings -> Allow this domain: userDomainReason returns {domain:'xn--55qx5d.cn', reason:null}, so an allow rule at 2,000,020 lets every malware host under 公司.cn through the threat tier. Today no packed threat host is an IDN suffix, so this is latent.
confirmed.evidence: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/idn.mjs output: '公司.cn xn--55qx5d.cn suffixReason= null protectedReason= null userAllow= {"domain":"xn--55qx5d.cn","reason":null}', same for 網絡.cn, 個人.hk, 政府.hk, 教育.hk, 公司.香港, ак.срб; compileThreatRules(['xn--55qx5d.cn','xn--55qx5d.hk']) returned one block rule and rejected []. Count of xn-- names in psl.js DATA.suffixes and privateSuffixes: 0 and 0. docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/gaps.mjs against the current PSL (VERSION 2026-11-15): 289 multi-label ICANN suffixes are threat-blockable; all except ad.vn, ap.vn, on.vn (newer PSL entries) are IDN.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In build-psl-subset.mjs, convert each Unicode label to punycode (for example new URL('http://' + rule.replace(/^[*!]\.?/, '') ).hostname, keeping the '*.' / '!' prefix) instead of skipping the line, then re-run the generator with a fresh PSL (this also picks up the about 60 private suffixes added since 2026-10-31, e.g. manus.space, prod.page, sanity.studio, auth.lovable.app). Add a test that suffixReason('xn--55qx5d.cn') and userDomainReason('公司.cn') refuse the name.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. psl.js has 0 'xn--' names because build-psl-subset.mjs:80 skips every non-ASCII PSL line instead of converting it to punycode. v.mjs shows that protectedReason('xn--55qx5d.cn') and protectedReason('xn--mxtq1m.hk') return null, isIcannSuffix returns false, compileThreatRules accepts xn--55qx5d.cn, and userDomainReason('公司.cn') returns {domain:'xn--55qx5d.cn', reason:null}. The 0.3.5 CHANGELOG adds IDN input to the allow box, which makes the allow side reachable. The impact is latent: no packed host is an IDN suffix, and a user must type an IDN suffix on purpose. So the severity is low, not medium.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The generator comment says 'PSL entries may be Unicode; DNR and URL hosts use punycode. Keep ASCII only.' The author knew the formats differ and chose to drop the lines rather than convert them, probably to avoid an IDNA dependency in the generator. The comment does not say that IDN suffixes are deliberately unprotected.
verdict.fix_notes: In scripts/build-psl-subset.mjs, for a non-ASCII line, keep the '*.'/'!' prefix, convert the rest with new URL('http://' + rest).hostname, and push the punycode rule. Skip the line only if the conversion throws. Re-run the generator with a fresh PSL, then rebuild threat-network.json and the packed general rules, because the ordinary tier's isIcannSuffix is also affected. Add tests: suffixReason('xn--55qx5d.cn') is non-null, userDomainReason('公司.cn').reason is non-null, and compileThreatRules(['xn--55qx5d.cn']) rejects it.

confirmed.title: Children of private PSL wildcard rules are not protected: a whole EC2 region (us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com) can be threat-blocked or allowed
confirmed.description: ruleSuffix() (psl.js:63-68) applies wildcard logic only to ICANN wildcard TLDs and ICANN wildcard bases. For PRIVATE wildcard rules the generator keeps only the base (build-psl-subset.mjs:113, 117), and the header says children of private wildcard rules are left out. But for '*.compute.amazonaws.com' and '*.compute.amazonaws.com.cn' each child is a regional namespace for every EC2 public DNS name in that region, the same blast radius that privateDeep explicitly protects for regional S3 endpoints ('A block on one would take out every bucket there'). The packed threat lists already name hosts in this namespace (Dandelion lines 1520-1523, ec2-...us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A list line ||us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com^ (for example a line cut short from ||ec2-54-177-49-112.us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com^) is accepted and blocks every EC2-hosted site and API reached by its ec2-*.us-west-1 name. In the other direction, a user who allows 'us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com' in the box (accepted, reason null) lets the packed malicious host ec2-54-177-49-112.us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com and every other bad EC2 host in that region through the threat tier.
confirmed.evidence: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/p4.mjs output: 'us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com null | allow-box: null', 'eu-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com null | allow-box: null', 'cn-north-1.compute.amazonaws.com.cn null | allow-box: null', but 'compute.amazonaws.com public suffix compute.amazonaws.com'. PSL has '*.compute.amazonaws.com' and '*.compute.amazonaws.com.cn' (lists/public_suffix_list.dat). Dandelion list lines 1520-1523 name ec2-*.us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com and ec2-*.compute-1.amazonaws.com hosts.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Emit private wildcard bases as their own set (privateWildcardBases) and let ruleSuffix() treat '<x>.<base>' as a suffix for them too (at least for bases under a PLATFORMS parent), so suffixReason() refuses region names. Add test cases for us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com and the allow box.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. protectedReason('us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com') returns null and the allow box accepts it, but compute.amazonaws.com is refused. PSL has '*.compute.amazonaws.com', so every '<region>.compute.amazonaws.com' is a public suffix. psl.js ruleSuffix() applies wildcard logic only to ICANN wildcardTlds and wildcardBases. In practice the risk is small: a list line naming a bare EC2 region is very unlikely, few real sites are reached by their ec2-* name, and a user would have to type a region name into the allow box on purpose.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The build-psl-subset.mjs header says: 'Left out: ... the children of PRIVATE wildcard rules.' docs/threat-tier.md says deeper rules are left out with 'UNVERIFIED blast radius, small'. The omission is documented and deliberate, for file size. But privateDeep already makes an exception for regional S3 endpoints for the same blast-radius reason, so the EC2 regions are an inconsistency.
verdict.fix_notes: In build-psl-subset.mjs, emit a new DATA.privateWildcardBases (bases of PRIVATE '*.' rules, at least those under a PLATFORMS parent, such as compute.amazonaws.com and compute.amazonaws.com.cn). In psl.js, use it in ruleSuffix() (labels.slice(1).join('.') in that set), or only in suffixReason() so isIcannSuffix stays ICANN-only. Add tests: protectedReason('us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com') and userDomainReason('eu-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com') are refused, and ec2-54-177-49-112.us-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com is still accepted.

confirmed.title: Popup drops clicks on No, Allow and Block again while the previous action waits for the worker, and gives no feedback
confirmed.description: guarded() keeps busy=true until the handler ends. Every handler ends with `await applyRules()`, which waits for the worker's applyGeneralState. That call runs in the worker's DNR queue (dnrExclusive), so a list swap, a threat-rule rebuild or a cold worker start can hold it for a long time. The handler calls render() before that await, so Yes/No, 'Block again' and the other buttons show as enabled. Only fixSite.disabled is set while busy (lines 447 and 310). A click during this time returns at `if (busy) return;` without a sound, a note or a disabled state. The applyRules wait is not needed for correctness, because the storage write already makes the worker run applyGeneralState through storage.onChanged (general-background.js:999-1007).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The worker DNR queue is busy (the 3-hourly list swap is running). The user clicks Fix this site. The question 'Did that fix it?' with Yes/No appears. The user clicks No. Nothing happens: the filters stay off, popupFix stays, and no note shows. The same thing happens when the user clicks Allow this site and then 'Block again' quickly: the second click is lost, and the site stays allowed.
confirmed.evidence: popup.js:443-455 `if (busy) return; busy = true; fixSite.disabled = true; try { await fn(); } finally { busy = false; render(); }`; popup.js:506-509 `await save(...); await refreshInfo(); render(); await applyRules();`. Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/busy-drop.test.mjs (it holds the applyGeneralState reply): output `after Fix: fix-ask hidden = false fix-no disabled = false focus = null` / `after No: overrides = {"news.example.com":{"features":{"cosmetic":false,...}}} note = "" popupFix present = true` / `Allow clicked while busy: overrides changed = false allow disabled = false`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not await applyRules inside the guarded section. Send it without waiting, after busy is cleared, or drop it, because storage.onChanged already applies the rules. As an alternative, disable every action button while busy is true, and do not only disable fixSite.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in the code. guarded() (popup.js:443-455) keeps busy=true until the handler returns. Every handler awaits applyRules() after render(), and the worker answers applyGeneralState only after dnrExclusive (general-background.js:429-430, 1191-1193), so the reply waits behind a list swap or a threat rebuild. During that wait render() has shown Yes/No and Block again as enabled, because only fixSite and undoFix read busy (popup.js:310-313). A click in that window returns at `if (busy) return;` and gives no feedback. The await is not needed: a siteOverrides write runs syncFromSettings (general-background.js:1007), which writes generalAllowedOrigins (lines 313-317), and that change runs applyGeneralState (lines 1001-1003). The existing repro busy-drop.test.mjs shows the dropped No click. Severity is low and not medium: no state is corrupted, the window is normally short (only the rule swap holds the queue, not the downloads), and the user sees the old state and can click again.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The guard is deliberate. CHANGELOG 0.3.5 line 20 says 'A double click on Fix this site no longer loses the earlier switch state', and the comment at popup.js:439-440 says a second click must not run on stale state. The await applyRules() probably makes sure the rules are in place before the user reloads. Nothing documents why busy must cover the worker round trip.
verdict.fix_notes: In popup.js, the handlers for allowSite, fixSite, fixNo and undoFixButton: do not await applyRules() inside the guarded section. Call it without await (void applyRules()) after the save, or drop it, because storage.onChanged already applies the rules. As an alternative, make render() set disabled=busy on allowSite, fixYes and fixNo too. Test: in a popup harness, hold the applyGeneralState reply. Click Fix, then click No. Expect the overrides to be restored and popupFix removed (or expect the No button to be disabled while busy).

confirmed.title: Keyboard focus is lost after Undo fix (and after Fix while the worker is slow)
confirmed.description: The Undo fix handler calls render() while busy is still true. render() sets `fixSite.disabled = !canFix || busy`, which is true. Then the handler calls fixSite.focus(). A disabled button cannot take focus, so the call does nothing. The Undo fix button that had focus is now hidden, so focus falls to <body>. When guarded() later enables fixSite, focus is already gone. The Fix handler has a related problem: guarded() disables fixSite while it has focus, and render() then hides it. fixYes.focus() runs only after `await applyRules()`. While the worker is slow, no element has focus.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A keyboard or screen reader user is on a site with a kept Fix, tabs to 'Undo fix' and presses Enter. The button disappears. Focus moves to the document body and does not go to 'Fix this site', so the user must tab again from the top of the popup. After Fix this site while the worker is busy, focus is also on body until the worker replies.
confirmed.evidence: popup.js:310 `fixSite.disabled = !canFix || busy;`; popup.js:571-576 `render(); await applyRules(); try { fixSite.focus(); }`. Repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/undo-focus.test.mjs (fake focus() refuses disabled or hidden nodes): `after Undo fix: activeElement = undo-fix undo hidden = true fix-site disabled now = false`, so the focus call was refused and focus stays on the now-hidden button. busy-drop.test.mjs prints `focus = null` after Fix.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Move focus after busy is cleared, for example in guarded()'s finally block after render(), using a target that the handler sets. You can also exclude busy from the disabled state of the focus target. Move focus before awaiting worker round trips.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. Undo fix is deterministic and does not need a slow worker. The handler calls render() while busy is still true, so fixSite.disabled = !canFix || busy = true (popup.js:310). Then the handler calls fixSite.focus() (popup.js:575), and a disabled button does not take focus. The Undo fix button that had focus becomes hidden, so focus falls to body. I re-ran docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/undo-focus.test.mjs and it prints 'activeElement = undo-fix undo hidden = true'. The Fix path has the same problem only while the worker is slow: fixYes.focus() runs after await applyRules().
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The focus calls show that the author wanted to keep keyboard focus (CHANGELOG 157 and 19 name keyboard-focus work). The busy-disabled state was added later for the double-click guard and was not checked against these focus calls. I found no reason for the current order.
verdict.fix_notes: In popup.js, let guarded() accept a focus target. Call it in the finally block after busy=false and render(). For example, the handler returns the element (fixSite, fixYes, allowSite) and finally calls el.focus() when !el.hidden && !el.disabled. Move the fixYes focus before any worker await. Test: in a harness whose focus() refuses disabled or hidden nodes, click Undo fix and expect activeElement to be fix-site. Click Fix with the applyGeneralState reply held and expect activeElement to be fix-yes before the reply comes.

confirmed.title: Settings page loses an earlier switch change when two changes overlap a slow storage write
confirmed.description: saveSettings() builds the new settings from the module-level `stored` snapshot, writes it, and refreshes `stored` only after `await set()` and `await load()`. A second change event that fires before the first write and reload finish reads the old snapshot. Its write then overwrites the first change. The same read-modify-write on a stale `stored` is in the Remove, Reset and Allow-add handlers (lines 190-191, 215-224, 284-286). storage.local writes are slow while the worker writes multi-MB list data, for example during Update lists.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user clicks Update lists. The worker writes list data. confirmed.title: Frozen-file gate (kick.js / Twitch vendor) cannot fail in the release workflow or on pushes to main
confirmed.description: Section 1b checks that src/kick.js and src/vendor/video-swap-new.user.js are unchanged by comparing the working tree with origin/main. In release.yml (which only runs on refs/heads/main) and in checks.yml on push to main, the checkout IS origin/main, so the diff is always empty and the check always passes. Nothing else pins src/kick.js. The Twitch file has a sha256 pin (scripts/vendor-pins.json, test/vendor-pin.test.js), but kick.js has no pin in any test. The freeze holds only if the PR release-gate job is a required status check and nobody pushes directly to main. The release workflow's own gate gives no protection.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A commit that applies docs/proposals/kick-0.3.5-fixes.patch (or any other kick.js edit) reaches main by a direct push or by an admin merge past a red PR check. Actions -> release -> Run workflow: section 1b prints 'PASS playback files match origin/main' and the release is published with the changed frozen file, without the owner decision that CHANGELOG 0.3.5 requires.
confirmed.evidence: release-gate.sh:258-283: BASE_REF=origin/main; `git -C "$PKG" diff --quiet "$BASE_REF" -- "$rel"`. Reproduction: clone into docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/clone, `echo '// changed' >> src/kick.js`, commit on main, `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD` (this is the state actions/checkout gives on main), `bash scripts/release-gate.sh` -> '=== 1b. Playback files untouched === PASS  playback files match origin/main (no content diff)'. grep found no sha256/digest pin for kick.js in test/.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pin the frozen files by content and do not compare them with a moving ref. Add src/kick.js (sha256 + bytes) to scripts/vendor-pins.json, or add a 'frozen' map there. In section 1b, compare sha256 of each PLAYBACK_FILES entry with the pin, in both repo mode and zip mode. Changing a pin then becomes an explicit, reviewable owner decision. Optionally, in release.yml also diff against the previous release tag (git describe --tags --abbrev=0).

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In release-gate.sh:258-283, BASE_REF is origin/main and the check is `git diff --quiet origin/main -- <file>`. release.yml runs only on refs/heads/main, and actions/checkout there gives a HEAD equal to origin/main, so section 1b can never fail in the release job or on the checks.yml push-to-main run. scripts/vendor-pins.json pins only the Twitch file. No test pins src/kick.js by digest. A grep of test/ for a kick sha256 or digest found nothing. The PR run of the release-gate job does catch the change. So the freeze holds only through branch protection or required checks, and the release gate itself adds no independent protection. Severity is low, not medium: the bypass needs a direct push or an admin merge past a red check.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The section is named 'Playback files untouched' and was written as a PR-diff guard (CHANGELOG 0.3.2: the release-gate job runs 'on every push to main and every pull request'). Comparing with origin/main is the natural check for a PR. The Twitch file later got a content pin (commit 90d256a) because it has a scripted updater. Nobody added the same pin for kick.js. No comment says that a moving-ref comparison is meant to be the only protection.
verdict.fix_notes: In scripts/vendor-pins.json, add a 'frozen' entry for src/kick.js with sha256 and bytes. In release-gate.sh section 1b, calculate the sha256 of each PLAYBACK_FILES entry, in repo mode and in zip mode, and compare it with the pin. Keep the origin/main diff as an extra check. Extend test/vendor-pin.test.js to check kick.js against the pin. A change to kick.js then needs a pin edit that the owner can review. Optionally, in release.yml also diff the frozen files against the previous release tag (git describe --tags --abbrev=0).

confirmed.title: List packer accepts an empty, HTML or truncated list body and silently drops that list from the shipped rules
confirmed.description: fetch() checks only that urlopen did not raise. The body is not checked: no '[Adblock' / '!' header, no minimum size, no comparison with the previous src/rules/meta.json per-source counts. extract_list() returns zero entries for an empty or HTML body. main() then merges, writes general-network.json, meta.json, packed-cross.json, LICENSES.md and the threat files, and exits 0. The runtime refresh (src/general/update.js checkListChange MAX_CHANGE_RATIO, and 'refreshed list too small' at update.js:1179) rejects exactly this case, but the build-time packer, whose output ships to every user, has no such guard. SENTINEL_HOSTS/sentinel_sources is only recorded, not enforced. Also, when a later step fails (build-threat-rules exit 2-5, pack-cosmetic exit 4), the packer has already rewritten general-network.json/meta.json, so the tree is left in a mixed state.
confirmed.failure_scenario: the owner runs `python3 scripts/pack-filter-lists.py` behind a captive portal or a CDN hiccup, and one source (for example easyprivacy or hagezi_pro_mini) answers HTTP 200 with an HTML page or an empty body. That list contributes 0 domains. general-network.json shrinks by tens of thousands of domains, meta.json records the new hash and counts, and the meta-count tests still pass because they check consistency, not size. The smaller ruleset ships in the next release. (The threat lists only fail later, after the general rules were already rewritten.)
confirmed.evidence: pack-filter-lists.py:609-622 (fetch: urlopen -> decode -> write cache, no content check). main() lines ~1181-1186 loop over sources with no count check. Reproduction: docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/packer_empty.py imports the packer and calls extract_list on '', on '<!DOCTYPE html>...Sign in to Wi-Fi...', and on a truncated EasyList head: all three give 'domains 0 scoped 0' with no exception. No test asserts per-source minimums: test/meta-counts.test.js only compares meta with the shipped file.
confirmed.suggested_fix: After each fetch, validate the body: a non-empty body, an Adblock/hosts header or a minimum line count, and no '<html' prefix. Before writing anything, compare each source's raw/kept count with the committed src/rules/meta.json and refuse (exit non-zero, nothing written) when a source shrinks by more than the runtime MAX_CHANGE_RATIO, unless a --accept-shrink flag is given. Build every output in a temp dir and move the files into place only after the threat and cosmetic steps succeed.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. fetch() in pack-filter-lists.py:609-622 accepts any HTTP 200 body. urlopen raises only on an HTTP error status. extract_list on an empty or HTML body gives 0 entries. main() then writes packed-cross.json, the blocks file, meta.json and the merged outputs, and nothing checks per-source counts against the committed meta.json. sentinel_sources is only recorded. test/no-openphish.test.js reads it, but only to check that dropped hosts do not ship, not to check list size. Severity is low, not medium. The packer runs only on the owner's machine, never in CI. The meta.json diff shows the shrink. Also, the runtime refresh downloads all lists after install and installs dynamic rules ('not on first load' for the 25% guard), so a shrunk packed list is replaced on the first online refresh.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The runtime refresh already has this guard (CHANGELOG 0.3.x: a list that grows or shrinks by more than 25% is rejected). The packer was treated as an attended local tool whose output the person checks by diff. I found no comment that says the packer leaves out this check on purpose.
verdict.fix_notes: In fetch(), refuse a body that is empty, starts with '<!doctype' or '<html', or has fewer than N lines. In main(), before write_packed_cross and before any other write, load the committed src/rules/meta.json and compare each source's raw and kept counts. Exit 1 with nothing written when a source shrinks by more than 25%, the same as the runtime MAX_CHANGE_RATIO, unless --accept-shrink is given. Add a Python unit test that gives main() a stubbed fetch with one empty source and expects a non-zero exit and no changed files.

confirmed.title: feed-sign.mjs signs feeds that are already expired (or not yet valid)
confirmed.description: The header says the script checks the file 'the way the extension will, so a file the extension would reject is not signed'. But it calls S.validateFeed(doc, { storedSerial: 0, now: Date.parse(doc.notBefore) }). Because 'now' is taken from the document's own notBefore, the checks 'now >= notAfter' (expired) and 'now < notBefore' (not valid yet) can never fire, and 'createdAt in the future' is judged against notBefore, not the real clock.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner signs a feed whose notAfter has already passed (for example a re-sign of an old file, or a date typo of 2025 for 2026). feed-sign exits 0 and writes a valid .sig. The extension rejects the uploaded feed ('feed expired'), so clients silently keep a stale snapshot. The signing step was meant to catch this.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduction in docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/feed/: feed-keygen --key-id t1 --out .../feed/k.json, then feed-sign on f.json with notBefore 2025-01-01, notAfter 2025-01-02 (today is 2026-11-16). Output: 'Signed feed/f.json (serial 5) with key id t1; wrote feed/f.json.sig', rc=0. schema.js:101-108 uses c.now for the expiry checks.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass now: Date.now() (optionally with a --now override for testing). Refuse to sign when notAfter is in the past or when notBefore is more than CLOCK_SKEW_MS in the future. Print a warning when fewer than 24 h of validity remain.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. feed-sign.mjs:36 passes now: Date.parse(doc.notBefore). In schema.js:101-108, the 'feed not valid yet' and 'feed expired' checks use c.now. With this value, 'now < notBefore' is always false, and 'now >= notAfter' is always false because the schema requires notAfter > notBefore. A feed that expired a year ago is signed with exit code 0. The header comment says a file the extension would reject is not signed, and that claim is wrong for expiry. The impact is small: the extension rejects the feed, and the client keeps its last verified copy or the packed snapshot. The feed is still dormant (FEED_ORIGIN is empty).
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: Using notBefore as 'now' probably lets the owner sign a feed ahead of time, with a future notBefore. This is a valid workflow, and the 'not valid yet' check must not block it. git log -S shows the line from the initial feed commit with no explanation. That reason does not apply to an already-expired notAfter.
verdict.fix_notes: In scripts/feed-sign.mjs, keep the notBefore-based validateFeed call for the schema checks. Then add a separate check against the real time: const real = Date.now() (with an optional --now override for tests). Refuse when notAfter <= real. Warn when notAfter - real < 24 h. Add a test in test/ that runs feed-sign on a feed with a past notAfter and expects a non-zero exit and no .sig file.

confirmed.title: release-gate --zip compares file names only, so a stale or edited zip passes as 'exactly the derived package files'
confirmed.description: In --zip mode the gate derives the file list from the checkout when the versions match (release-gate.sh:216-231), but --check-zip compares only the set of names. A zip packed before later commits (for example a list repack or a code fix at the same manifest version) is reported CLEAN, and the PASS line suggests that the zip matches the tree. verdict.reason: Confirmed. package_files.py:201-213 compares only the set of names. Gate sections 1-4 then check the zip's own contents, which are consistent with themselves. A zip packed before a later same-version commit passes as 'exactly the derived package files'. release.yml always packs a fresh zip from the checkout in the same job, so the CI release path is not affected. The risk is only in the local flow (TODO.md records manual runs of release-gate.sh --zip) and in uploads that are not done through the release workflow, for example to the Chrome Web Store.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: The comment at release-gate.sh:211-215 says the check is about the file set: optional files must not be smuggled in. For each zip entry, compare sha256(z.read(name)) with sha256 of root/name, and fail with 'zip is not a pack of this checkout: <file>'. In release-gate.sh, pass the flag when DERIVE_ROOT is ROOT. confirmed.title: uBO sync runs upstream gorhill/uBlock code with -A from a mutable tag and never verifies the recorded commit
confirmed.description: The script clones gorhill/uBlock at --branch 1.75.0 (a tag) and then dynamically imports three of its JS modules (lines 42-44) under `deno run -A` (full file, net, env and run access), both on the owner's PC and in the weekly CI job. src/vendor/ubo-youtube-meta.json records ublock_commit 21f0e686..., but the script never compares the cloned HEAD with it. A re-pointed or compromised tag runs arbitrary code with full permissions. The Twitch vendor update, by contrast, pins and verifies a commit and sha256 and never executes upstream code.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Tag 1.75.0 on gorhill/uBlock is moved (or the clone is redirected) to a commit whose static-filtering-parser.js reads ~/.ssh or environment variables and posts them out. The next local `deno run -A scripts/sync-ubo-youtube.mjs` executes it with full rights. In CI the job has contents:read only, but the code still runs unrestricted.
confirmed.evidence: Line 25: `const uboTag = arg("--ubo", "1.75.0")`. Line 32: `git clone -q --depth 1 --branch ${uboTag}`. Line 33: uboCommit is only read, not checked. Lines 42-44: `await import(`file://${tmp}/ubo/src/js/...`)`. ubo-youtube.yml: `deno run -A scripts/sync-ubo-youtube.mjs`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pin the uBO commit (for example in scripts/vendor-pins.json, from the meta's ublock_commit). After cloning, fail when `git rev-parse HEAD` is different, unless --ubo-commit is given explicitly. Replace -A with explicit grants (--allow-read=<repo>,<tmp> --allow-write=<repo>/src,<tmp> --allow-net=raw.githubusercontent.com --allow-run=git).

verdict.reason: Confirmed. sync-ubo-youtube.mjs:25 uses the tag 1.75.0 by default. Line 32 clones that tag. Line 33 reads HEAD but never compares it with ublock_commit in src/vendor/ubo-youtube-meta.json. Today, the generated scriptlets from that repo ship to users anyway, so trust in upstream is part of the design. The extra risk is full-permission code on the owner's PC and in CI. confirmed.title: Identity/secret scan exclusion '--glob !src/rules/*' is dead because the gate passes absolute paths

The '!src/rules/*' glob therefore matches nothing, and the multi-MB list data (general-network.json, cosmetic-rules.json, packed-cross.json) is scanned. confirmed.title: Docs say the permissions are 'exactly' 3 APIs plus list hosts, but content scripts on http://*/* and https://*/* give all-sites access. This is not disclosed or justified anywhere.
confirmed.description: README.md:85 and docs/permissions-and-privacy.md:9 say the permissions are 'exactly storage, declarativeNetRequest, alarms, and the listed hosts (all for downloading public filter lists)'. But manifest.json content_scripts entries at lines 140, 221 and 271 match "http://*/*" and "https://*/*". Two of them run in the MAIN world, in all frames, with match_about_blank and match_origin_as_fallback. Chrome counts content-script match patterns as host access. So the install prompt shows 'Read and change all your data on all websites', and the Chrome Web Store dashboard requires a host-permission justification for that access. No doc mentions this: a search for 'all websites', 'Read and change', 'site access' and 'warning' over README.md, docs/permissions-and-privacy.md, docs/how-it-works.md and docs/STORE-REVIEW-NOTES.md found nothing. STORE-REVIEW-NOTES.md covers only the vendored eval. The docs also do not say what happens when the user limits Site access in chrome://extensions ('On click' or 'On specific sites'). Then cosmetic.js, flags.js and the clipboard and pop-up guards do not inject, so the ClickFix guard is silently off. The popup (src/popup.js:298) gets no pageOrigin answer and tells the user 'Open a normal http(s) page... Already on one? Reload it.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: 1) A store submission uses the docs' permission list as its justification. The reviewer sees the all-sites content-script access, which the justification does not mention, and the submission can be rejected or sent to in-depth review. 2) A user installs the extension after reading 'permissions are exactly ... all for downloading public filter lists', then sees Chrome's 'Read and change all your data on all websites' prompt, which the docs did not mention. 3) A privacy-minded user sets Site access to 'On specific sites'. On every other site the clipboard guard does not run, and no UI says so. The popup only says to reload.

README.md:85: "exactly `storage`, `declarativeNetRequest`, `alarms`, and the listed hosts (all for downloading public filter lists)". docs/permissions-and-privacy.md:9 says the same. grep -i 'read and change|all your data|site access|warning' over the docs: no hits.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In README and permissions-and-privacy.md, say that the content scripts need access to all http(s) sites (hide rules and page guards), and that Chrome shows this as 'Read and change all your data on all websites'. Add a host-permission justification paragraph to docs/STORE-REVIEW-NOTES.md. Document what happens under restricted Site access. If possible, let the popup tell 'no host access' apart from 'page opened before install', for example with chrome.permissions.contains on the page origin when the URL is known.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. manifest.json has three content_scripts entries that match http://*/* and https://*/* (cosmetic.js; flags.js; the MAIN-world clipboard and pop-up guards with all_frames true). Chrome counts content-script matches as host access, so the install prompt shows 'Read and change all your data on all websites'. README.md:85 and docs/permissions-and-privacy.md:9 say the permissions are 'exactly' storage, declarativeNetRequest, alarms and the listed hosts, 'all for downloading public filter lists'. The 'Host permissions' section lists only the 9 list hosts. No doc says that this site access exists or why it is needed, and STORE-REVIEW-NOTES.md covers only the vendored eval. The popup text for 'no host access' (popup.js:286 path, origin empty) is the same as for 'page opened before install'. This is a disclosure gap. It is not a runtime bug.

TODO.md:40 says no store submission was made yet.

confirmed.title: EasyList material is stated as redistributed under CC BY-SA 3.0, but the packer merges it into the same DNR rules as GPL-3.0-only and 'non-commercial' list data
confirmed.description: LICENSES.md:92-95 chooses the CC BY-SA 3.0-or-later option of EasyList's dual licence. scripts/pack-filter-lists.py merge_domains() (line 992) builds one domain list from all sources (EasyList, EasyPrivacy, AdGuard Base GPL-3.0, HaGeZi GPL-3.0, uBO badware GPL-3.0, Peter Lowe 'free for personal/non-commercial use') and cuts it into 80-domain rules (all 2,852 list rules have priority 1, line 1058). So each shipped rule can hold domains from several licences. CC BY-SA 3.0 and GPL-3.0 are not compatible with each other (only CC BY-SA 4.0 is one-way compatible into GPLv3), and a 'non-commercial' term is a further restriction that GPLv3 section 10 does not allow. EasyList is also offered under GPL-3.0-or-later, so the wrong option is chosen. The Peter Lowe term (LICENSES.md:33) is not reconciled with the GPLv3 project LICENSE either.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A downstream redistributor or a store/legal review reads LICENSES.md. general-network.json is said to be CC BY-SA 3.0 for the EasyList part, but the same file and the same rules hold GPL-3.0-only data. No single licence can cover the merged file as LICENSES.md describes it.

"priority": 1 ...}); python count of general-network.json: 2852 rules with priority 1.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Choose the GPL-3.0-or-later option for EasyList and EasyPrivacy in LICENSES.md, CREDIT-EasyList.txt and LICENSE-EasyList.txt. Then all merged network data except Peter Lowe is GPL-3.0. Ask the owner to check Peter Lowe's current terms, then either note an explicit permission or keep that list's domains in rules of their own with a separate licence note.

confirmed.title: The shipped-rules hCaptcha check cannot fail for a regexFilter and does not see subdomain urlFilters
confirmed.description: The test 'shipped block rules name no hCaptcha host' does the last check on the shipped rulesets. Line 243 first changes each '\.' to '.' in regexFilter. Then it tests the result against /hcaptcha\\.com/. That regex needs a literal backslash, and the replace removed all of them. Thus the assert passes for all single-escaped regexFilters. Line 241 (urlFilter) matches only '||hcaptcha.com' or '||*.hcaptcha.com' at the start. It does not see '||sentry.hcaptcha.com/...', '||stats.hcaptcha.com' or '|https://hcaptcha.com/...'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A list pack ships a block rule {regexFilter: '^https?://([a-z]+\\.)?hcaptcha\\.com/'} or {urlFilter: '||sentry.hcaptcha.com/1/api.js'}. Captcha widgets then break on sites. This test stays green. The packer filter scripts/merge-dnr-rules.py drop_hcaptcha_filter_rules is the only remaining guard, and the tests run it only on synthetic input.
confirmed.evidence: Checked in this session: repro docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/hcaptcha-shipped-guard.mjs copies lines 241 and 243 without change. Output: all 4 regexFilter cases print 'not caught: true'. 3 of 4 urlFilter cases print 'not caught: true'. Only '||hcaptcha.com^' is caught. grep found no other hCaptcha regexFilter scan of the shipped JSON in scripts/release-gate.sh. Not checked: whether a shipped rule today names hCaptcha (the test passes, but it is blind).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not unescape. Compile each regexFilter with new RegExp(rf, 'i') and test it against probe URLs (https://hcaptcha.com/1/api.js, https://sentry.hcaptcha.com/x, https://imgs.hcaptcha.com/captcha). For urlFilter, use the dnr-matcher urlFilterToRegExp with the same probes. Add a self-test with one positive case for each branch.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In test/hcaptcha-never-block.test.js:243 the code first changes each '\.' in the regexFilter to '.'. Then it tests the result against /hcaptcha\\.com/, and that regex needs a literal backslash, so it can never match. Line 241 matches only '||hcaptcha.com' or '||*.hcaptcha.com' at the start of the filter. My own repro (docs/review-2026-11-16/repros/verify-tests-quality/h.mjs) gave 'caught: false' for '^https?://([a-z]+\.)?hcaptcha\.com/', 'hcaptcha\.com', '||sentry.hcaptcha.com/1/api.js' and '|https://hcaptcha.com/'. It gave 'caught: true' only for '||hcaptcha.com^'. No shipped rule uses a high-priority allow rule as a fallback for hCaptcha, and isNeverBlock filters only dynamic list data, not the static rulesets. The shipped rulesets today have no hCaptcha block (I scanned all 3: the only hit is ubo-youtube rule 4, and there hcaptcha.com is in excludedRequestDomains). The defect is therefore latent. The packer filter (merge-dnr-rules.py drop_hcaptcha_filter_rules) is the primary guard, so I rate this medium, not high.
verdict.why_it_may_be_intentional: No reason found. The replace step is meant to make the check tolerate escaping, but it removes the backslashes that the next regex then requires. CHANGELOG 0.3.5 says hcaptcha.com and its subdomains are never blocked in the packed lists. That shows the test intends to cover subdomains and regexFilters.
verdict.fix_notes: In the test 'shipped block rules name no hCaptcha host': do not unescape and do not match the regexFilter text. For each block rule, compile the regexFilter with new RegExp(rf, 'i'). Test it against the probe URLs https://hcaptcha.com/1/api.js, https://sentry.hcaptcha.com/x, https://imgs.hcaptcha.com/captcha and https://newassets.hcaptcha.com/c. For a urlFilter, export urlFilterToRegExp from test/fixtures/dnr-matcher.js (or use ruleMatches with each probe and the type 'script'), so that the requestDomains, excludedRequestDomains and urlFilter are all applied together. Add self-tests: one synthetic regexFilter rule and one '||sentry.hcaptcha.com^' rule must be caught, and a 'nothcaptcha.com' rule must not be caught.

confirmed.title: No test catches an alarm refresh that never refetches an expired list (listDue)
confirmed.description: listDue decides if an automatic refresh downloads a list again after its '! Expires' time.
